1.2.s:
manugarbhadaśāyāṃ tu pitṛdevarṣimānavāḥ |
iti sṛṣṭāstayā śaśvadvidyayā brahmaṇā svayam || 7-57 ||
1.2.d:
मनुगर्भदशायां तु पितृदेवर्षिमानवाः |
इति सृष्टास्तया शश्वद्विद्यया ब्रह्मणा स्वयम् || 7-57 ||
1.2.m: During the state of the Manus being embryos, however, the ancestors, gods, sages, and humans / are created perpetually by that Vidyā, by Brahmā himself. // 7-57
The Manus, gods, and others being individual components of the immoveable Puruṣa

1.2.s:
kūṭastho yaḥ purā proktaḥ pumān vyomnaḥ parādadhaḥ |
manavo devatādyāśca tadvyaṣṭaya itīritāḥ || 7-58 ||
1.2.d:
कूटस्थो यः पुरा प्रोक्तः पुमान् व्योम्नः परादधः |
मनवो देवताद्याश्च तद्व्यष्टय इतीरिताः || 7-58 ||
1.2.m: The immoveable Puruṣa who was described earlier below the supreme space— / the Manus, deities, and others are declared to be his individual components. // 7-58
The individual souls being manifestations of the Lord's becoming
All distinct individual souls, O sage, are fashioned from portions of Viṣṇu's becoming.
Transformation of the Intellect into the form of a cloud

1.2.s: atha vyakteṣu manuṣu prajāteṣu punaḥ punaḥ || 7-59 ||
1.2.d: अथ व्यक्तेषु मनुषु प्रजातेषु पुनः पुनः || 7-59 ||
1.2.m: Then, when the Manus were manifested and produced repeatedly, // 7-59

1.2.s:
vidyaivāṃśena kenāpi dhenurbhavati śāśvatī |
dhenurityucyate vidyā meghabhāvamupāgatā || 7-60 ||
1.2.d:
विद्यैवांशेन केनापि धेनुर्भवति शाश्वती |
धेनुरित्युच्यते विद्या मेघभावमुपागता || 7-60 ||
1.2.m: Vidyā itself, through some portion, becomes the eternal milch cow; / Vidyā, having attained the state of a cloud, is called 'the milch cow.' // 7-60
She yields milk called rain, which undergoes transformation into grain and other [food].
Statement of the cause of the loss of knowledge in individual souls

1.2.s: tattu vaidyaṃ payaḥ prāśya sarve mānavamānavāḥ || 7-61 ||
1.2.d: तत्तु वैद्यं पयः प्राश्य सर्वे मानवमानवाः || 7-61 ||
1.2.m: Having drunk that milk originating from Vidyā, all the human-descendants of Manu, // 7-61

1.2.s: jñānabhraṃśaṃ prapadyante sarvajñāḥ svata eva te |
1.2.d: ज्ञानभ्रंशं प्रपद्यन्ते सर्वज्ञाः स्वत एव ते |
1.2.m: though naturally omniscient, undergo a loss of knowledge.
Then the setting in motion of sacred teaching
Then the sacred teaching is set in motion by the firstborn Manus at that time. // 7-62

1.2.s:
tadādiṣṭena mārgeṇa te yānti paramāṃ gatim |
leśataḥ sṛṣṭirukteyaṃ bhūteḥ śuddhetarā mune || 7-63 ||
1.2.d:
तदादिष्टेन मार्गेण ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् |
लेशतः सृष्टिरुक्तेयं भूतेः शुद्धेतरा मुने || 7-63 ||
1.2.m: By the path taught by that [sacred teaching], they go to the supreme state. / This, O sage, has been declared in brief: the creation other than pure belonging to becoming, // 7-63
which is brought into being in this manner by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana.
Summary of the meaning of the two chapters
Listen further, O Nārada, to this summary in truth: // 7-64

1.2.s:
ekā śaktirharerviṣṇoḥ sarvabhāvānugāminī |
devī ṣāḍguṇyapūrṇā sā jñānānandakriyāmayī || 7-65 ||
1.2.d:
एका शक्तिर्हरेर्विष्णोः सर्वभावानुगामिनी |
देवी षाड्गुण्यपूर्णा सा ज्ञानानन्दक्रियामयी || 7-65 ||
1.2.m: The single power of Hari, of Viṣṇu, follows every state of being; / she is the goddess filled with the six qualities, consisting of knowledge, bliss, and action. // 7-65

1.2.s:
bhāvyabhāvakabhedena sā dvidhābhāvamṛcchati |
bhāvakastatra saṃkalpaḥ sudarśanamayo hareḥ || 7-66 ||
1.2.d:
भाव्यभावकभेदेन सा द्विधाभावमृच्छति |
भावकस्तत्र संकल्पः सुदर्शनमयो हरेः || 7-66 ||
1.2.m: Through the division into that which is brought into being and that which brings into being, she undergoes a twofold state; / that which brings into being therein is Hari's resolve, consisting of Sudarśana. // 7-66

1.2.s:
avyāghātastu yastasya sā sudarśanatā mune |
jñānamūlakriyātmāsau svacchaḥ svacchandacinmayaḥ || 7-67 ||
1.2.d:
अव्याघातस्तु यस्तस्य सा सुदर्शनता मुने |
ज्ञानमूलक्रियात्मासौ स्वच्छः स्वच्छन्दचिन्मयः || 7-67 ||
1.2.m: And that which is his non-obstruction, that, O sage, is the state of being Sudarśana; / consisting of action rooted in knowledge, it is clear, composed of free consciousness. // 7-67

1.2.s:
bhāvyo nāma parāṃśo yaḥ sā bhūtiriti gīyate |
saṃkarṣaṇādibhūmyantā śuddhetaravibhāginī || 7-68 ||
1.2.d:
भाव्यो नाम परांशो यः सा भूतिरिति गीयते |
संकर्षणादिभूम्यन्ता शुद्धेतरविभागिनी || 7-68 ||
1.2.m: That which is the other part, called that which is brought into being, is celebrated as becoming; / ending with the earth from Saṃkarṣaṇa onwards, it is divided into the pure and the other than pure. // 7-68

1.2.s:
saṃkarṣaṇādivyūhāntā śuddhasargamayī sthitā |
śaktyādirbhūmiparyantā śuddhetaramayī mune || 7-69 ||
1.2.d:
संकर्षणादिव्यूहान्ता शुद्धसर्गमयी स्थिता |
शक्त्यादिर्भूमिपर्यन्ता शुद्धेतरमयी मुने || 7-69 ||
1.2.m: Ending with the emanations from Saṃkarṣaṇa onwards, it consists of pure creation; / beginning with Śakti and ending with the earth, O sage, it consists of what is other than pure. // 7-69

1.2.s:
aṃśayoḥ puruṣo madhye yaḥ sthitaḥ sa caturyugaḥ |
śuddhetaramayaṃ viddhi kūṭasthaṃ taṃ mahāmune || 7-70 ||
1.2.d:
अंशयोः पुरुषो मध्ये यः स्थितः स चतुर्युगः |
शुद्धेतरमयं विद्धि कूटस्थं तं महामुने || 7-70 ||
1.2.m: The Puruṣa who stands in the middle between the two parts is four-yoked; / know him, the immoveable Puruṣa, O great sage, to consist of what is other than pure. // 7-70

1.2.s:
itīyaṃ vividhā bhūtirnānātattvamayī mune |
sudarśanena marutā jvāleva bahudheryate || 7-71 ||
1.2.d:
इतीयं विविधा भूतिर्नानातत्त्वमयी मुने |
सुदर्शनेन मरुता ज्वालेव बहुधेर्यते || 7-71 ||
1.2.m: Thus this manifold becoming, consisting of diverse principles, O sage, / is set in motion in many ways by Sudarśana, like a flame by the wind. // 7-71

1.2.s:
ānulomyena sarge tu prātilomyena cāpyaye |
madhye ca sthāpyate tena kāryate ca tathā tathā || 7-72 ||
1.2.d:
आनुलोम्येन सर्गे तु प्रातिलोम्येन चाप्यये |
मध्ये च स्थाप्यते तेन कार्यते च तथा तथा || 7-72 ||
1.2.m: In direct order during creation, but in reverse order during dissolution, / and in the middle, it is maintained by him and caused to act in various ways. // 7-72
The worthlessness of an entity independent of Sudarśana

1.2.s:
bhūteraṃśaḥ sa naivāsti svalpālpo'pi mahāmune |
yo na yāti svajanmādau sudarśanavidheyatām || 7-73 ||
1.2.d:
भूतेरंशः स नैवास्ति स्वल्पाल्पोऽपि महामुने |
यो न याति स्वजन्मादौ सुदर्शनविधेयताम् || 7-73 ||
1.2.m: There is no part of becoming at all, O great sage, even the smallest of the small, / that does not, in its arising and the like, undergo subservience to Sudarśana. // 7-73

1.2.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
śuddhetarasṛṣṭivarṇanaṃ nāma saptamo'dhyāyaḥ || 7 ||
1.2.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
शुद्धेतरसृष्टिवर्णनं नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः || 7 ||
1.2.m: Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'Description of Creation Other than Pure', in the Ahirbudhnya Saṃhitā of the esoteric Tantra of the glorious Pāñcarātra. // 7
The eighth chapter, named 'Ascertainment of the Support of the World'
Manifold disagreement of disputants concerning creation

1.2.s:
bhagavan devadevaśa bhaganetravināśana |
śrutaṃ mayaitadakhilaṃ tava vaktrāmbujasrutam || 8-1 ||
1.2.d:
भगवन् देवदेवश भगनेत्रविनाशन |
श्रुतं मयैतदखिलं तव वक्त्राम्बुजस्रुतम् || 8-1 ||
1.2.m: O Lord, ruler of the gods of gods, destroyer of the eyes of Bhaga! / All this has been heard by me, flowing from your lotus-mouth. // 8-1

1.2.s:
vyākulastvantarātmā me nānājñānavimohitaḥ |
kecit traibhūtikīṃ sṛṣṭiṃ bruvate tattvavādinaḥ || 8-2 ||
1.2.d:
व्याकुलस्त्वन्तरात्मा मे नानाज्ञानविमोहितः |
केचित् त्रैभूतिकीं सृष्टिं ब्रुवते तत्त्ववादिनः || 8-2 ||
1.2.m: Yet my inner self is agitated, deluded by diverse doctrines: / some disputants on the principles speak of a creation consisting of three elements; // 8-2

1.2.s:
caturbhūtamayīmanye ke'pyanye pāñcabhautikīm |
tāṃ ṣaḍdhātumayīmeke saptadhātumayīṃ pare || 8-3 ||
1.2.d:
चतुर्भूतमयीमन्ये केऽप्यन्ये पाञ्चभौतिकीम् |
तां षड्धातुमयीमेके सप्तधातुमयीं परे || 8-3 ||
1.2.m: others, of one consisting of four elements; still others, of one consisting of five elements; / some, of it as consisting of six constituents; others, of it as consisting of seven constituents; // 8-3
some, of it having eight evolvents; others, of it having nine evolvents; / some, of it as consisting of ten principles; some, as consisting of eleven; // 8-4

1.2.s:
evamuccāvacāṃ saṃkhyāṃ tattvaprakṛtigocarām |
vadanti munayaḥ siddhā devā vedāstathaiva ca || 8-5 ||
1.2.d:
एवमुच्चावचां संख्यां तत्त्वप्रकृतिगोचराम् |
वदन्ति मुनयः सिद्धा देवा वेदास्तथैव च || 8-5 ||
1.2.m: thus sages, perfected beings, gods, and likewise the Vedas / proclaim high and low numbers concerning the domain of principles and evolvents. // 8-5

1.2.s:
aṇḍajāmapare sṛṣṭiṃ padmajāmapi cāpare |
pāvakīmapare sṛṣṭiṃ kecit kāyāntarodbhavām || 8-6 ||
1.2.d:
अण्डजामपरे सृष्टिं पद्मजामपि चापरे |
पावकीमपरे सृष्टिं केचित् कायान्तरोद्भवाम् || 8-6 ||
1.2.m: Others [call] creation born from an egg, and others born from a lotus; / others [call] creation born of fire, some arisen from another body; // 8-6
some, consisting of the womb of knowledge; and others, having the nature of the void.
Question arising from the desire to know the truth in this regard
In this way, those high and low teachings in the great ocean of diverse scriptures, // 8-7
which is turbulent with the clamour produced by the billows of diverse philosophical systems— / sunken in it, this boatless intellect of mine is bewildered today. // 8-8
Rescue it, O Śaṃkara, by granting the raft of decisive conclusion!
Beginning of the answer to that

1.2.s: ucitaṃ tava devarṣe yadayaṃ praśna īritaḥ || 8-9 ||
1.2.d: उचितं तव देवर्षे यदयं प्रश्न ईरितः || 8-9 ||
1.2.m: It is fitting of you, O divine sage, that this question has been raised. // 8-9

1.2.s:
muhyantyatra mahānto'pi śṛṇu me tattvanirṇayam |
paramātmā paro deva ekaḥ ṣāḍguṇyamujjvalam || 8-10 ||
1.2.d:
मुह्यन्त्यत्र महान्तोऽपि शृणु मे तत्त्वनिर्णयम् |
परमात्मा परो देव एकः षाड्गुण्यमुज्ज्वलम् || 8-10 ||
1.2.m: Even the great are deluded here; listen to my determination of the truth: / The Supreme Self is the supreme deity, one, radiant with the six qualities. // 8-10
The inability of even the words of the Veda to fathom the truth completely

1.2.s:
vāganādiranantāpi tattvaṃ tannāvagāhate |
guṇaistaṭasthitaistaistairajānāneva sā sthitā || 8-11 ||
1.2.d:
वागनादिरनन्तापि तत्त्वं तन्नावगाहते |
गुणैस्तटस्थितैस्तैस्तैरजानानेव सा स्थिता || 8-11 ||
1.2.m: Speech, though beginningless and endless, does not fathom that truth; / by means of those various marginal qualities, it remains as if not knowing. // 8-11
Statement of the cause of the disagreement

1.2.s:
yadguṇe nāmni ye śrāntāstatra tattvavido mune |
manubhistadguṇaistaistaiste te tattvavidāṃ varāḥ || 8-12 ||
1.2.d:
यद्गुणे नाम्नि ये श्रान्तास्तत्र तत्त्वविदो मुने |
मनुभिस्तद्गुणैस्तैस्तैस्ते ते तत्त्वविदां वराः || 8-12 ||
1.2.m: Those knowers of truth, O sage, who have laboured over that name in which a [particular] quality resides, / they, the best among knowers of truth, through the Manus possessing those various qualities, // 8-12
indicate the cause of the world, O great sage, by words established by themselves; / by those [words] caused by manifold qualities, uttered by diverse speakers, // 8-13
people who do not understand synonyms remain divided.
Lakṣmī's being the referent of diverse words, though she is one

1.2.s: evaṃ viṣṇoḥ priyā bhāḥ sā śaktiḥ ṣāḍguṇyavigrahā || 8-14 ||
1.2.d: एवं विष्णोः प्रिया भाः सा शक्तिः षाड्गुण्यविग्रहा || 8-14 ||
1.2.m: Thus, that beloved splendour of Viṣṇu, the power whose body is the six qualities, // 8-14
though one, is worshipped by knowers of truth by means of diverse names.
The knowers of truth propounding what each has personally perceived
When she goes forth in creation by her own resolve, // 8-15

1.2.s:
tathā nivartamānāyāṃ svasaṃkalpena saṃhṛtau |
vijñānabalavaiṣamyādye ye tattvavido mune || 8-16 ||
1.2.d:
तथा निवर्तमानायां स्वसंकल्पेन संहृतौ |
विज्ञानबलवैषम्याद्ये ये तत्त्वविदो मुने || 8-16 ||
1.2.m: and likewise when she returns in withdrawal by her own resolve— / owing to differences in the power of comprehension, whichever knowers of truth, O sage, // 8-16

1.2.s:
nyūnādhikavibhedena yāvatīrdadṛśurbhidāḥ |
tāvatīstāvatīste te procuḥ śiṣyābhicoditāḥ || 8-17 ||
1.2.d:
न्यूनाधिकविभेदेन यावतीर्ददृशुर्भिदाः |
तावतीस्तावतीस्ते ते प्रोचुः शिष्याभिचोदिताः || 8-17 ||
1.2.m: saw however many divisions according to lesser or greater distinctions, / each of them proclaimed precisely that many, when questioned by their disciples. // 8-17

1.2.s:
ataścāsarvadṛgbuddhiḥ saṃkhyāsu pravimuhyati |
pitāmahādayo ye ca jagatkāryādhikāriṇaḥ || 8-18 ||
1.2.d:
अतश्चासर्वदृग्बुद्धिः संख्यासु प्रविमुह्यति |
पितामहादयो ये च जगत्कार्याधिकारिणः || 8-18 ||
1.2.m: Hence, an intellect that does not see everything is bewildered concerning numbers. / And those who are appointed to the work of the world, such as the Grandfather [Brahmā]— // 8-18

1.2.s:
teṣāṃ nyūnādhibhāvo'pi vaktṛbhedāt prakalpitaḥ |
svātantryamaniyojyaṃ tu viṣṇoḥ ṣāḍguṇyarūpiṇaḥ || 8-19 ||
1.2.d:
तेषां न्यूनाधिभावोऽपि वक्तृभेदात् प्रकल्पितः |
स्वातन्त्र्यमनियोज्यं तु विष्णोः षाड्गुण्यरूपिणः || 8-19 ||
1.2.m: even their lesser or greater status is formulated according to differences among speakers; / but the sovereignty of Viṣṇu, whose form is the six qualities, cannot be called into question. // 8-19
From the variety of his intellect's inclination arises the egg, the lotus, and the like; / the activities of the Supreme Self do not brook questioning. // 8-20
The endlessness of the Lord's modes

1.2.s:
sa yathā ceṣṭate sṛṣṭau sthitau saṃharaṇe'pi vā |
tathā tathā prakārāste hyanantāḥ kālavaibhavāt || 8-21 ||
1.2.d:
स यथा चेष्टते सृष्टौ स्थितौ संहरणेऽपि वा |
तथा तथा प्रकारास्ते ह्यनन्ताः कालवैभवात् || 8-21 ||
1.2.m: According as he acts in creation, in preservation, or in withdrawal, / so those modes are indeed endless owing to the power of time. // 8-21
Disputants propounding only single modes

1.2.s:
evaṃ prakāranānātve devasya harimedhasaḥ |
kaścidekaṃ paro'nyaṃ tu prakāramaparo'param || 8-22 ||
1.2.d:
एवं प्रकारनानात्वे देवस्य हरिमेधसः |
कश्चिदेकं परोऽन्यं तु प्रकारमपरोऽपरम् || 8-22 ||
1.2.m: Thus, when there is a manifoldness of modes of the deity whose intelligence is Hari, / one [thinker], having known through his intellect one mode, another another, and another yet another, // 8-22
proclaimed it to a disciple out of a desire for his welfare.
Hence the diversity of sacred teachings
Hence, such is the varied operation of scriptures on creation and the like. // 8-23
Just as at present for humans, the apportionment of pleasure and pain / in divisions such as day and night arises from the variation of action, // 8-24
so the apportionment of pleasure and pain is accepted in the days of Brahmā.
The multiformity of the cosmic eons of Brahmā
Some days of Brahmā are troubled by storms, O best of sages; // 8-25

1.2.s:
tathā varṣākulāḥ kecit kecidātapasaṃkulāḥ |
prabhūtaśatravaḥ kecit kecit susvamanoharāḥ || 8-26 ||
1.2.d:
तथा वर्षाकुलाः केचित् केचिदातपसंकुलाः |
प्रभूतशत्रवः केचित् केचित् सुस्वमनोहराः || 8-26 ||
1.2.m:
likewise some are troubled by rains, some are choked with heat,
some have abundant enemies, and some are delightful to their own. // 8-26

1.2.s:
anena niścayenaiva dhiyamāsthāya śāśvatīm |
saṃstambhayāntarātmānaṃ vyāmohaste vinaśyatu || 8-27 ||
1.2.d:
अनेन निश्चयेनैव धियमास्थाय शाश्वतीम् |
संस्तम्भयान्तरात्मानं व्यामोहस्ते विनश्यतु || 8-27 ||
1.2.m:
Taking recourse to an eternal understanding with this very certainty,
steady your inner self; let your perplexity perish! // 8-27

1.2.s:
p. 77) iti nānāvidhākāraṃ kriyābhūtivibheditam |
nimittotpādakākāraṃ kāraṇaṃ kathitaṃ mune || 8-28 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 77) इति नानाविधाकारं क्रियाभूतिविभेदितम् |
निमित्तोत्पादकाकारं कारणं कथितं मुने || 8-28 ||
1.2.m:
Thus the cause having multiform aspect, differentiated into action and becoming,
having the form of the efficient and the material cause, has been related, O sage. // 8-28

1.2.s:
kāraṇaṃ kathitaṃ deva sarvajña vṛṣaketana |
yā sā śaktirjagaddhātuḥ kathitā samavāyinī || 8-29 ||
1.2.d:
कारणं कथितं देव सर्वज्ञ वृषकेतन |
या सा शक्तिर्जगद्धातुः कथिता समवायिनी || 8-29 ||
1.2.m:
The cause has been described, O lord, all-knowing one who has a bull on his banner!
That inherent power of the creator of the world which was described, // 8-29

1.2.s:
lakṣmīrnāma dvidhā sā tu kriyābhūtivibhedinī |
yā kriyā nāma saṃkalpaḥ sa sudarśananāmavān || 8-30 ||
1.2.d:
लक्ष्मीर्नाम द्विधा सा तु क्रियाभूतिविभेदिनी |
या क्रिया नाम संकल्पः स सुदर्शननामवान् || 8-30 ||
1.2.m:
called Lakṣmī, is twofold, dividing into action and becoming.
That which is action is volition; it bears the name Sudarśana. // 8-30

1.2.s:
bhūtirnāma jagadrūpā kālāvyaktapumātmikā |
aśuddhā śuddharūpā tu sā vyūhavibhavātmikā || 8-31 ||
1.2.d:
भूतिर्नाम जगद्रूपा कालाव्यक्तपुमात्मिका |
अशुद्धा शुद्धरूपा तु सा व्यूहविभवात्मिका || 8-31 ||
1.2.m:
Becoming consists of the universe, made of time, the Unmanifest, and Puruṣa;
that is impure, but its pure form consists of the emanations and divine descents. // 8-31

1.2.s:
kriyā pravartikā bhūteḥ sā sudarśanarūpiṇī |
ityetaddarśitaṃ tattvaṃ devadevena me śrutam || 8-32 ||
1.2.d:
क्रिया प्रवर्तिका भूतेः सा सुदर्शनरूपिणी |
इत्येतद्दर्शितं तत्त्वं देवदेवेन मे श्रुतम् || 8-32 ||
1.2.m:
Action is the instigator of becoming; it has the form of Sudarśana.
Thus this reality demonstrated by the God of gods has been heard by me. // 8-32
Reminder of the second question

1.2.s:
adhunā śrotumicchāmi dvitīyaṃ praśnamīśvara |
ādhāro nāma yaḥ prokto jagatāṃ vṛṣabhadhbaja || 8-33 ||
1.2.d:
अधुना श्रोतुमिच्छामि द्वितीयं प्रश्नमीश्वर |
आधारो नाम यः प्रोक्तो जगतां वृषभध्बज || 8-33 ||
1.2.m:
Now I wish to hear the second question, O Lord,
concerning that which is taught as the support of the worlds, O bull-bannered one! // 8-33
Sudarśana as the support of the universe

1.2.s:
śṛṇu nārada tattvena ya ādhāra udīryate |
yenedaṃ dhriyate viśvaṃ tantunā maṇayo yathā || 8-34 ||
1.2.d:
शृणु नारद तत्त्वेन य आधार उदीर्यते |
येनेदं ध्रियते विश्वं तन्तुना मणयो यथा || 8-34 ||
1.2.m:
Listen, Nārada, to that which is called the support in truth,
by which this universe is held, like gems upon a thread. // 8-34

1.2.s:
p. 78) yā sā śaktirharerādyā lakṣmīrnāma mahāmune |
yā sā sarvātmano viṣṇorbhāvābhāvānuyāyinī || 8-35 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 78) या सा शक्तिर्हरेराद्या लक्ष्मीर्नाम महामुने |
या सा सर्वात्मनो विष्णोर्भावाभावानुयायिनी || 8-35 ||
1.2.m:
That primordial power of Hari called Lakṣmī, O great sage,
which follows the existence and non-existence of Viṣṇu, who is the Self of all, // 8-35

1.2.s:
tasyā alpāyutāṃśāṃśaḥ svasvātantryavijṛmbhitaḥ |
kriyābhūtivibhedena samudetīti varṇitam || 8-36 ||
1.2.d:
तस्या अल्पायुतांशांशः स्वस्वातन्त्र्यविजृम्भितः |
क्रियाभूतिविभेदेन समुदेतीति वर्णितम् || 8-36 ||
1.2.m:
a minute fraction of a myriadth part of her, bursting forth by its own autonomy,
arises divided into action and becoming—so it has been described. // 8-36

1.2.s:
sudarśanena kriyayā śaṅkuneva chado mune |
bhūtiḥ sā dhriyate śaśvadvistaraṃ tatra me śṛṇu || 8-37 ||
1.2.d:
सुदर्शनेन क्रियया शङ्कुनेव छदो मुने |
भूतिः सा ध्रियते शश्वद्विस्तरं तत्र मे शृणु || 8-37 ||
1.2.m:
By Sudarśana as action, as a canopy by a pole, O sage,
that becoming is continually held; hear from me the details thereof. // 8-37
Therein, the first: the wheel bearing the Great Night

1.2.s:
saṃhṛtākhilabhūtasya staimityaṃ brahmaṇo hi yat |
apyayaḥ sā mahārātristatsaṃkalpena dhāryate || 8-38 ||
1.2.d:
संहृताखिलभूतस्य स्तैमित्यं ब्रह्मणो हि यत् |
अप्ययः सा महारात्रिस्तत्संकल्पेन धार्यते || 8-38 ||
1.2.m:
The motionlessness of Brahman when all beings are withdrawn,
that dissolution is the Great Night; it is held by his volition. // 8-38

1.2.s:
mahārātridharo nāma tadaraṃ vai sudarśanam |
tadekāraṃ mahaccakramadyatve cintyate suraiḥ || 8-39 ||
1.2.d:
महारात्रिधरो नाम तदरं वै सुदर्शनम् |
तदेकारं महच्चक्रमद्यत्वे चिन्त्यते सुरैः || 8-39 ||
1.2.m:
Sudarśana, bearing the Great Night, is indeed its spoke.
That great one-spoked wheel is meditated upon by the gods even now. // 8-39

1.2.s:
yat sisṛkṣāmayaṃ rūpaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śaktisaṃbhavam |
jvāleva vāyunā vahneḥ saṃkalpena tadīryate || 8-40 ||
1.2.d:
यत् सिसृक्षामयं रूपं ब्रह्मणः शक्तिसंभवम् |
ज्वालेव वायुना वह्नेः संकल्पेन तदीर्यते || 8-40 ||
1.2.m:
That form of Brahman consisting of the desire to create, born of power,
is stirred by volition like a flame of fire by the wind. // 8-40

1.2.s:
uṣaścakraṃ taduddiṣṭamaradvitayabhūṣitam |
bhūtikāmairajasraṃ tadbrahmaṇā caiva dhāryate || 8-41 ||
1.2.d:
उषश्चक्रं तदुद्दिष्टमरद्वितयभूषितम् |
भूतिकामैरजस्रं तद्ब्रह्मणा चैव धार्यते || 8-41 ||
1.2.m:
That is indicated as the wheel of dawn, adorned with two spokes;
it is continually held by Brahman and by those desiring prosperity. // 8-41

1.2.s:
yaḥ sa saṃkarṣeṇonmeṣo yo dhārayati taṃ sadā |
sākṣādudayacakraṃ tadvijñānatritayātmakam || 8-42 ||
1.2.d:
यः स संकर्षेणोन्मेषो यो धारयति तं सदा |
साक्षादुदयचक्रं तद्विज्ञानत्रितयात्मकम् || 8-42 ||
1.2.m:
The awakening that belongs to Saṃkarṣaṇa, which continually holds it,
is the actual wheel of sunrise, consisting of a triad of special cognitions. // 8-42
That volition of Saṃkarṣaṇa is attended upon by those desiring knowledge.
The fourth: the wheel of sovereignty

1.2.s: yaḥ sa prādyumna unmeṣa aiśvaryamaya ūrjitaḥ || 8-43 ||
1.2.d: यः स प्राद्युम्न उन्मेष ऐश्वर्यमय ऊर्जितः || 8-43 ||
1.2.m: That awakening belonging to Pradyumna, consisting of sovereignty, is mighty; // 8-43

1.2.s:
vaiṣṇavenaiva lākṣmeṇa sa saṃkalpena dhāryate |
tadvai pradyumnasaṃkalpamaiśvaryamayamūrjitam || 8-44 ||
1.2.d:
वैष्णवेनैव लाक्ष्मेण स संकल्पेन धार्यते |
तद्वै प्रद्युम्नसंकल्पमैश्वर्यमयमूर्जितम् || 8-44 ||
1.2.m:
it is held by that very Vaiṣṇava volition belonging to Lakṣmī.
That volition of Pradyumna is indeed powerful and consists of sovereignty. // 8-44
Those established in sovereignty worship the complete four-spoked wheel.
The fifth: the great wheel of power
That awakening belonging to Aniruddha, illumined by power and splendour, // 8-45

1.2.s:
saṃkalpo brahmaśaktyutthastaṃ dhārayati sarvadā |
tadvaiśaktimahācakraṃ pañcāraṃ parikalpitam || 8-46 ||
1.2.d:
संकल्पो ब्रह्मशक्त्युत्थस्तं धारयति सर्वदा |
तद्वैशक्तिमहाचक्रं पञ्चारं परिकल्पितम् || 8-46 ||
1.2.m:
the volition arising from the power of Brahman always holds it.
That is conceived as the great wheel of power, possessing five spokes. // 8-46
The All-gods worship it for the sake of abundance of power and splendour.
The group of twelve beginning with Keśava is proclaimed as the sub-emanations; // 8-47

1.2.s:
sudarśanena dhriyate yena saṃkalparūpiṇā |
ṣaḍaraṃ tanmahācarkaṃ vyūhāntaravibhāvakam || 8-48 ||
1.2.d:
सुदर्शनेन ध्रियते येन संकल्परूपिणा |
षडरं तन्महाचर्कं व्यूहान्तरविभावकम् || 8-48 ||
1.2.m:
by which Sudarśana in the form of volition it is held,
that six-spoked great wheel manifests the sub-emanations. // 8-48

1.2.s: p. 80) ṛtvaraṃ tat samākhyātaṃ vratakāmā upāsate |
1.2.d: प्. 80) ऋत्वरं तत् समाख्यातं व्रतकामा उपासते |
1.2.m: It is declared to have the seasons as its spokes; those desiring vows worship it.
The seventh: the Mahāsudarśana wheel
The mighty divine descent previously described, beginning with Padmanābha, // 8-49

1.2.s:
sa yena dhriyate viṣṇoḥ saṃkalpena mahāmune |
mahāsudarśanaṃ nāma dvādaśāraṃ taducyate || 8-50 ||
1.2.d:
स येन ध्रियते विष्णोः संकल्पेन महामुने |
महासुदर्शनं नाम द्वादशारं तदुच्यते || 8-50 ||
1.2.m:
by which volition of Viṣṇu it is held, O great sage,
is called Mahāsudarśana, having twelve spokes. // 8-50

1.2.s:
vibhavāntarasaṃjñaṃ tadyacchaktyāveśasaṃbhavam |
dhṛtaṃ tad dvādaśāreṇa tatsaṃkalpena cakriṇā || 8-51 ||
1.2.d:
विभवान्तरसंज्ञं तद्यच्छक्त्यावेशसंभवम् |
धृतं तद् द्वादशारेण तत्संकल्पेन चक्रिणा || 8-51 ||
1.2.m:
That designated as secondary divine descents, arising from possession by power,
is held by the discus-wielder through that twelve-spoked volition of his. // 8-51
The eighth: the thousand-spoked wheel

1.2.s:
yattu tat paramaṃ vyoma yad viṣṇoḥ padamūrjitam |
sahasrāreṇa cakreṇa tatsaṃkalpena dhāryate || 8-52 ||
1.2.d:
यत्तु तत् परमं व्योम यद् विष्णोः पदमूर्जितम् |
सहस्रारेण चक्रेण तत्संकल्पेन धार्यते || 8-52 ||
1.2.m:
That which is supreme space, the mighty abode of Viṣṇu,
is held by that volition of his by means of the thousand-spoked wheel. // 8-52

1.2.s:
ete saudarśanā vyūhāḥ samāsena prakīrtitāḥ |
ādhārādheyabhāvena vartante te svayaṃ mune || 8-53 ||
1.2.d:
एते सौदर्शना व्यूहाः समासेन प्रकीर्तिताः |
आधाराधेयभावेन वर्तन्ते ते स्वयं मुने || 8-53 ||
1.2.m:
These emanations of Sudarśana have been proclaimed in brief;
they themselves exist, O sage, in the relationship of support and supported. // 8-53

1.2.s:
saṃkalpaḥ koṭikoṭyaṃśaḥ śakterbhūtistathā dvidhā |
śaktiḥ sā vaiṣṇavī sattā bahudhaivaṃ prabhāsate || 8-54 ||
1.2.d:
संकल्पः कोटिकोट्यंशः शक्तेर्भूतिस्तथा द्विधा |
शक्तिः सा वैष्णवी सत्ता बहुधैवं प्रभासते || 8-54 ||
1.2.m:
Volition is a fraction of a hundred-millionth part of power, and becoming is twofold;
that power, the existence belonging to Viṣṇu, shines forth in many ways thus. // 8-54

1.2.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
jagadādhāravarṇanaṃ nāma aṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ || 8 ||
1.2.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
जगदाधारवर्णनं नाम अष्टमोऽध्यायः || 8 ||
1.2.m:
Thus ends the eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Support of the Universe',
in the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā of the esoteric teaching of the Pāñcarātra. // 8
Chapter nine, named 'Determination of the Support of the Impure Universe'
The first: the wheel of Puruṣa

1.2.s:
ādhāraḥ kathitaḥ śuddhaḥ śuddhā sā yena dhāryate |
bhūtirvyūhādirūpeṇa yā sā devī pravartate || 9-1 ||
1.2.d:
आधारः कथितः शुद्धः शुद्धा सा येन धार्यते |
भूतिर्व्यूहादिरूपेण या सा देवी प्रवर्तते || 9-1 ||
1.2.m:
The pure support has been described, by which the pure is held,
[namely] becoming in the form of the emanations and the like, as which that goddess proceeds. // 9-1

1.2.s:
pumādyavaniparyantā yathā śuddhetarātmikā |
sā yena dhāryate cakraṃ tatsaṃkalpamayaṃ śṛṇu || 9-2 ||
1.2.d:
पुमाद्यवनिपर्यन्ता यथा शुद्धेतरात्मिका |
सा येन धार्यते चक्रं तत्संकल्पमयं शृणु || 9-2 ||
1.2.m:
Hear how the wheel consisting of his volition holds that
which is other than pure, from Puruṣa down to the earth. // 9-2

1.2.s: tryaraṃ tat pauruṣaṃ cakraṃ puruṣo yena dhāryate |
1.2.d: त्र्यरं तत् पौरुषं चक्रं पुरुषो येन धार्यते |
1.2.m: The three-spoked wheel is that of Puruṣa, by which Puruṣa is held.

1.2.s: cakraṃ triṃśadaraṃ proktaṃ śaktiḥ sā yena dhāryate || 9-3 ||
1.2.d: चक्रं त्रिंशदरं प्रोक्तं शक्तिः सा येन धार्यते || 9-3 ||
1.2.m: A thirty-spoked wheel is proclaimed, by which that power is held. // 9-3

1.2.s:
tādṛśaṃ naiyataṃ cakraṃ niyatiryena dhāryate |
ṣaḍaraṃ kālacakraṃ tat sa kālo yena dhāryate || 9-4 ||
1.2.d:
तादृशं नैयतं चक्रं नियतिर्येन धार्यते |
षडरं कालचक्रं तत् स कालो येन धार्यते || 9-4 ||
1.2.m:
Such is the wheel of Destiny, by which Destiny is held;
that wheel of time has six spokes, by which time is held. // 9-4

1.2.s:
sattvaṃ rajastamaścaiva dhāryante yairmahāmune |
tāni tvādhāracakrāṇi tryarāṇīti vidurbudhāḥ || 9-5 ||
1.2.d:
सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चैव धार्यन्ते यैर्महामुने |
तानि त्वाधारचक्राणि त्र्यराणीति विदुर्बुधाः || 9-5 ||
1.2.m:
By which [wheels] goodness, passion, and darkness are held, O great sage,
the wise know those supporting wheels to be three-spoked. // 9-5

1.2.s: cakramekādaśāraṃ tu buddhiḥ sā yena dhāryate |
1.2.d: चक्रमेकादशारं तु बुद्धिः सा येन धार्यते |
1.2.m: The wheel is eleven-spoked by which the intellect is held.
That great eight-spoked wheel is the holder of egoity. // 9-6

1.2.s:
ekāraṃ vaiyataṃ cakraṃ dvyaraṃ tadvāyudhārakam |
tryaraṃ taijasamākhyātamāpyaṃ caturaraṃ mune || 9-7 ||
1.2.d:
एकारं वैयतं चक्रं द्व्यरं तद्वायुधारकम् |
त्र्यरं तैजसमाख्यातमाप्यं चतुररं मुने || 9-7 ||
1.2.m:
The wheel of space has one spoke; that which holds wind has two spokes;
the fiery is proclaimed three-spoked, and the watery four-spoked, O sage; // 9-7

1.2.s:
pañcāraṃ pārthivaṃ cakraṃ pṛthivī yena dhāryate |
guṇacakrāṇyaraiḥ sarvāṇyaṅkitāni tribhistribhiḥ || 9-8 ||
1.2.d:
पञ्चारं पार्थिवं चक्रं पृथिवी येन धार्यते |
गुणचक्राण्यरैः सर्वाण्यङ्कितानि त्रिभिस्त्रिभिः || 9-8 ||
1.2.m:
the earthy wheel by which the earth is held has five spokes.
All the wheels of the qualities are marked with three spokes each. // 9-8

1.2.s:
ekādaśavidhaṃ cakramaindriyaṃ dviyugārakam |
iyamādhāraśaktiste proktā pratisvikī mune || 9-9 ||
1.2.d:
एकादशविधं चक्रमैन्द्रियं द्वियुगारकम् |
इयमाधारशक्तिस्ते प्रोक्ता प्रतिस्विकी मुने || 9-9 ||
1.2.m:
The wheel of the faculties is elevenfold, having four spokes.
This individual supporting power has been declared to you, O sage. // 9-9

1.2.s:
ekadhāraṃ mahaccakraṃ mahābhūtikaraṃ śṛṇu |
mahāketupaṭī yadvadvitatā vyomni dhāryate || 9-10 ||
1.2.d:
एकधारं महच्चक्रं महाभूतिकरं शृणु |
महाकेतुपटी यद्वद्वितता व्योम्नि धार्यते || 9-10 ||
1.2.m:
Hear of the single-rimmed great wheel which causes great manifestation:
Just as a vast banner-cloth spread out in the sky is held // 9-10

1.2.s:
aniśaṃ pāvamānena pavamānena vai mune |
saṃkarṣaṇādibhūmyantā viṣṇuśaktimayī tathā || 9-11 ||
1.2.d:
अनिशं पावमानेन पवमानेन वै मुने |
संकर्षणादिभूम्यन्ता विष्णुशक्तिमयी तथा || 9-11 ||
1.2.m:
incessantly by the purifying wind, O sage,
even so the becoming, consisting of the power of Viṣṇu, beginning with Saṃkarṣaṇa and ending with the earth, // 9-11

1.2.s:
nirālambe paṭe bhūtiḥ saṃkalpenaiva dhāryate |
tatsaṃkalpamayaṃ cakramanantāraṃ mahāmune || 9-12 ||
1.2.d:
निरालम्बे पटे भूतिः संकल्पेनैव धार्यते |
तत्संकल्पमयं चक्रमनन्तारं महामुने || 9-12 ||
1.2.m:
is held upon the supportless cloth by [His] mere will.
That wheel consisting of His will has endless spokes, O great sage: // 9-12

divine, called the Great Manifestation, transcending speech and mind,
immeasurable, without beginning or end, characterized by being and non-being, // 9-13

infinitely spoked, boundless, crowded with bounded aggregates,
brought to light by hundreds of millions and billions of floods of crores of cosmic eggs, // 9-14

causing the manifestation of floods of thousands upon thousands of gross elements,
with faculties by the tens of millions having the lustre of fireflies, // 9-15

marked and variegated with cosmic eggs resembling tiny clouds,
spread out somewhere as if with waters consisting of the gross elements, // 9-16

1.2.s:
vipruṅbhiriva varṣāṇāṃ vitataṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ padam |
mahābhūtaiḥ kvaciddīptaṃ jyotirbhirayutāyutaiḥ || 9-17 ||
1.2.d:
विप्रुङ्भिरिव वर्षाणां विततं वैष्णवं पदम् |
महाभूतैः क्वचिद्दीप्तं ज्योतिर्भिरयुतायुतैः || 9-17 ||
1.2.m:
spread out like the raindrops of the monsoon—the realm of Viṣṇu;
blazing in places with myriads upon myriads of gross elements as lights, // 9-17

fanned somewhere by elemental breezes as if raised by fans,
pierced by spaces by the tens of millions resembling tiny openings, // 9-18

egotized by egoities of various forms,
marked by Intellects small and great dividing into tens of millions, // 9-19

made dense with forms of darkness of diverse types,
colored somewhere by myriads upon myriads of passions shifting through diverse torments, // 9-20

1.2.s:
rajobhī rañjitaṃ kṣudrairviśadairlaghubhiḥ kvacit |
aṅkitaṃ bahubhiḥ sattvairvimalaiḥ koṭikoṭiśaḥ || 9-21 ||
1.2.d:
रजोभी रञ्जितं क्षुद्रैर्विशदैर्लघुभिः क्वचित् |
अङ्कितं बहुभिः सत्त्वैर्विमलैः कोटिकोटिशः || 9-21 ||
1.2.m:
marked somewhere by minute, bright, light,
and pure goodnesses in their tens of millions; // 9-21

by times threefold, of six varieties, divided into two sets of six,
into twenty-four divisions, shining with two sets of fifteen, // 9-22

crowded with sixty-six divisions, dividing into tens of millions,
manifold in many thousands and dense with myriads upon myriads; // 9-23

1.2.s:
p. 84) kīrṇaṃ niyatirūpeṇa nānāniyamanātmanā |
koṭikoṭisahasraughakoṭikoṭiguṇena ca || 9-24 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 84) कीर्णं नियतिरूपेण नानानियमनात्मना |
कोटिकोटिसहस्रौघकोटिकोटिगुणेन च || 9-24 ||
1.2.m:
strewn with the form of Destiny consisting of various ordainments,
multiplied by floods of thousands of tens of millions; // 9-24

with a power having the nature of honeycombs of various forms,
with drops of honey whose intrinsic nature is a flowing flood of principles; // 9-25

taking forms in myriads, hundreds of thousands, and floods of thousands of tens of millions;
somewhere exceedingly smooth as it were, somewhere occupied by Puruṣa as it were, // 9-26

possessing forms fashioned by actions of white, red, and black appearance,
its nature resembling an udumbara fruit filled with many gnats, // 9-27

through the variety of manifold living beings, enjoying various apportionments of fruit,
its nature tangled with the latent impressions of both auspicious and inauspicious forms, // 9-28

occupied in some places by the Puruṣa, a sheath of many afflictions,
and [elsewhere] consisting of pure blissful awareness and great existence; // 9-29

by eternal, liberated, untroubled souls characterized by spotless bliss,
who behold directly the healthy Lord Nārāyaṇa, // 9-30

1.2.s:
devyā lakṣmyā samāsīnaṃ pūrṇaṣāḍguṇyadehayā |
nityoditairnityatṛptairatikrāntaistamo mahat || 9-31 ||
1.2.d:
देव्या लक्ष्म्या समासीनं पूर्णषाड्गुण्यदेहया |
नित्योदितैर्नित्यतृप्तैरतिक्रान्तैस्तमो महत् || 9-31 ||
1.2.m:
seated together with Goddess Lakṣmī, whose body is full with the six divine attributes—
constantly elevated, eternally satisfied, having transcended the great darkness; // 9-31

1.2.s:
ātmabhiḥ śobhitenaivaṃ vareṇa niyatāṅkitam |
ṣāḍguṇyavigrahairvyūhaiḥ puruṣaiḥ puṣkarekṣaṇaiḥ || 9-32 ||
1.2.d:
आत्मभिः शोभितेनैवं वरेण नियताङ्कितम् |
षाड्गुण्यविग्रहैर्व्यूहैः पुरुषैः पुष्करेक्षणैः || 9-32 ||
1.2.m:
thus adorned with the supreme self, constantly distinguished
by the lotus-eyed Puruṣas, the emanations whose bodies are the six divine attributes, // 9-32

1.2.s:
p. 85) āsthitaṃ jagadutpattisthitisaṃhṛtikāribhiḥ |
iti vyāptavatīmetāṃ vibhūtiṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ parām || 9-33 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 85) आस्थितं जगदुत्पत्तिस्थितिसंहृतिकारिभिः |
इति व्याप्तवतीमेतां विभूतिं वैष्णवीं पराम् || 9-33 ||
1.2.m:
who preside over it and cause the origin, preservation, and destruction of the universe.
Thus, this supreme power of Viṣṇu has pervaded [all this]; // 9-33

1.2.s:
citrāmbaradharāṃ samyagdadhadātmānamātmanā |
saṃkalpo vaiṣṇavo yo'yaṃ maṇīn sūtramivāsthitaḥ || 9-34 ||
1.2.d:
चित्राम्बरधरां सम्यग्दधदात्मानमात्मना |
संकल्पो वैष्णवो योऽयं मणीन् सूत्रमिवास्थितः || 9-34 ||
1.2.m:
wearing variegated garments, duly upholding itself by itself,
this will of Viṣṇu resides [within all] like a string through gems. // 9-34

1.2.s:
tadanantāramavyaktaṃ mahaccakraṃ sudarśanam |
bhāvitaṃ smṛtimātreṇa bhāvayatyakhilā gatīḥ || 9-35 ||
1.2.d:
तदनन्तारमव्यक्तं महच्चक्रं सुदर्शनम् |
भावितं स्मृतिमात्रेण भावयत्यखिला गतीः || 9-35 ||
1.2.m:
That great unmanifest Sudarśana wheel of endless spokes,
when meditated upon, brings about all paths of progress by mere remembrance. // 9-35

1.2.s:
yo jihīrṣāmayo nityaḥ saṃkalpo vaiṣṇavaḥ paraḥ |
anantāramaparyantaṃ tatsaṃhṛtisudarśanam || 9-36 ||
1.2.d:
यो जिहीर्षामयो नित्यः संकल्पो वैष्णवः परः |
अनन्तारमपर्यन्तं तत्संहृतिसुदर्शनम् || 9-36 ||
1.2.m:
The supreme, eternal will of Viṣṇu that consists of the desire to withdraw [all things]
is the Sudarśana of dissolution, infinitely spoked and boundless. // 9-36

1.2.s:
eka eva tu saṃkalpo rūpairnānopagīyate |
anantamaparicchedyamaprameyamanūpamam || 9-37 ||
1.2.d:
एक एव तु संकल्पो रूपैर्नानोपगीयते |
अनन्तमपरिच्छेद्यमप्रमेयमनूपमम् || 9-37 ||
1.2.m:
Yet the will is only one, though sung of in various forms:
endless, indeterminable, immeasurable, incomparable. // 9-37

1.2.s:
ataraṅgārṇavākāramanabhrāmbarasaṃnibham |
ekaṃ tat paramaṃ brahma ṣāḍguṇyastimitaṃ mahat || 9-38 ||
1.2.d:
अतरङ्गार्णवाकारमनभ्राम्बरसंनिभम् |
एकं तत् परमं ब्रह्म षाड्गुण्यस्तिमितं महत् || 9-38 ||
1.2.m:
Resembling a waveless ocean, like a cloudless sky,
that one supreme Brahman is great, motionlessly resting in the six divine attributes. // 9-38

1.2.s:
bhāvābhāvamayī tasya śaktirekānapāyinī |
taddharmadharmiṇī divyā jyotsneva himadīdhiteḥ || 9-39 ||
1.2.d:
भावाभावमयी तस्य शक्तिरेकानपायिनी |
तद्धर्मधर्मिणी दिव्या ज्योत्स्नेव हिमदीधितेः || 9-39 ||
1.2.m:
His single, unperishing power consists of existence and non-existence,
possessing His attributes as its property, divine like the moonlight of the cool-rayed moon. // 9-39

1.2.s:
tasya saṃkalpasaṃkalpo rūpavyāpriyamāṇatā |
staimityasthitisaṃkalpastimitaṃ tat sudarśanam || 9-40 ||
1.2.d:
तस्य संकल्पसंकल्पो रूपव्याप्रियमाणता |
स्तैमित्यस्थितिसंकल्पस्तिमितं तत् सुदर्शनम् || 9-40 ||
1.2.m:
The willing of His will is its occupation with forms;
when the will rests in motionlessness, that Sudarśana is motionless. // 9-40

1.2.s:
prabhave cāpyaye vāpi sthitau vāpi mahāmune |
calattāpūrvarūpaṃ yaḥ saṃkalpastatra vartate || 9-41 ||
1.2.d:
प्रभवे चाप्यये वापि स्थितौ वापि महामुने |
चलत्तापूर्वरूपं यः संकल्पस्तत्र वर्तते || 9-41 ||
1.2.m:
In origination, in dissolution, or in preservation, O great sage,
whatever will operates there, preceded by movement, // 9-41
that great wheel consisting of Sudarśana is called Movement.
Three divisions of it are to be known by those who have crossed to the further shore of knowledge of the scriptures: // 9-42

1.2.s:
mahāsṛṣṭimayaṃ tatra samāsavyāsalakṣaṇam |
nānāśaktisamākīrṇaṃ tacca te kathitaṃ purā || 9-43 ||
1.2.d:
महासृष्टिमयं तत्र समासव्यासलक्षणम् |
नानाशक्तिसमाकीर्णं तच्च ते कथितं पुरा || 9-43 ||
1.2.m:
Among these, that which consists of the great creation, characterized by contraction and expansion,
and filled with various powers, has already been explained to you. // 9-43

1.2.s:
mahāsaṃhāracakraṃ ca samāsavyāsalakṣaṇam |
tādṛgevātra vijñeyaṃ tacca te darśitaṃ purā || 9-44 ||
1.2.d:
महासंहारचक्रं च समासव्यासलक्षणम् |
तादृगेवात्र विज्ञेयं तच्च ते दर्शितं पुरा || 9-44 ||
1.2.m:
And the wheel of great withdrawal, characterized by contraction and expansion,
is to be known as just the same here; and that too has already been shown to you. // 9-44

1.2.s:
sthiticakraṃ tu yanmadhye samāsavyāsalakṣaṇam |
tasya vakṣyāmi vistāraṃ yatpramāṇatayā sthitam || 9-45 ||
1.2.d:
स्थितिचक्रं तु यन्मध्ये समासव्यासलक्षणम् |
तस्य वक्ष्यामि विस्तारं यत्प्रमाणतया स्थितम् || 9-45 ||
1.2.m:
Now I shall explain the extent of the wheel of preservation that stands in the middle,
characterized by contraction and expansion, according to its authoritative measure. // 9-45

1.2.s:
yathā hyeko naṭo bhāvairnānārūpairvibhajyate |
tathā saṃkalpa evaikastaistairbhedairvibhajyate || 9-46 ||
1.2.d:
यथा ह्येको नटो भावैर्नानारूपैर्विभज्यते |
तथा संकल्प एवैकस्तैस्तैर्भेदैर्विभज्यते || 9-46 ||
1.2.m:
For just as a single actor is divided into various roles by different states,
so the single will is divided by those various divisions. // 9-46

1.2.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
aśuddhajagadādhāranirūpaṇaṃ nāma navamo'dhyāyaḥ || 9 ||
1.2.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
अशुद्धजगदाधारनिरूपणं नाम नवमोऽध्यायः || 9 ||
1.2.m: Thus ends the ninth chapter, entitled "Ascertainment of the Support of the Impure Universe", in the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā in the esoteric teaching of the Pāñcarātra. // 9
Chapter Ten, entitled "Ascertainment of the Authoritative Means of Knowledge Consisting of Objects"

1.2.s:
bhagavan devadeveśa bhavānījīviteśvara |
lokanātha jagannātha devānāmabhayaprada || 10-1 ||
1.2.d:
भगवन् देवदेवेश भवानीजीवितेश्वर |
लोकनाथ जगन्नाथ देवानामभयप्रद || 10-1 ||
1.2.m:
O Blessed One, Lord of the gods of gods, Lord of the life of Bhavānī,
Protector of the world, Lord of the universe, Bestower of fearlessness upon the gods! // 10-1

1.2.s:
namaste tripuraghnāya tattvavijñānasindhave |
daśāvyayāya te nityaṃ ṣaḍaṅgāya namo namaḥ || 10-2 ||
1.2.d:
नमस्ते त्रिपुरघ्नाय तत्त्वविज्ञानसिन्धवे |
दशाव्ययाय ते नित्यं षडङ्गाय नमो नमः || 10-2 ||
1.2.m:
Homage to you, slayer of Tripura, ocean of the knowledge of the principles!
To you who are ten-limbed and imperishable, who have six limbs, homage, homage forever! // 10-2

1.2.s:
yadetaduditaṃ nityaṃ jagatkāraṇamavyayam |
yaccādhāratayā proktaṃ saṃkalpākhyaṃ sudarśanam || 10-3 ||
1.2.d:
यदेतदुदितं नित्यं जगत्कारणमव्ययम् |
यच्चाधारतया प्रोक्तं संकल्पाख्यं सुदर्शनम् || 10-3 ||
1.2.m:
That eternal, imperishable cause of the universe which has been declared,
and that which was spoken of as the substratum, namely Sudarśana called Will, // 10-3

1.2.s:
tadetadakhilaṃ deva viṣṇusaṃkalpajṛmbhitam |
samāsavyāsarūpeṇa tattvato me'vadhāritam || 10-4 ||
1.2.d:
तदेतदखिलं देव विष्णुसंकल्पजृम्भितम् |
समासव्यासरूपेण तत्त्वतो मेऽवधारितम् || 10-4 ||
1.2.m:
all that, O god, is an unfolding of Viṣṇu's will.
I have comprehended it in truth in the form of contraction and expansion. // 10-4

1.2.s:
idānīṃ śrotumicchāmi vistareṇāntakāntaka |
kiṃ tat pramāṇamityuktaṃ kīdṛśaṃ kiṃvidhaṃ ca tat || 10-5 ||
1.2.d:
इदानीं श्रोतुमिच्छामि विस्तरेणान्तकान्तक |
किं तत् प्रमाणमित्युक्तं कीदृशं किंविधं च तत् || 10-5 ||
1.2.m:
Now I wish to hear in detail, O slayer of Antaka:
What is that which is called measure? Of what nature and of what kind is it? // 10-5

1.2.s:
kimarthaṃ kiṃmayaṃ deva tanme vistaraśo vada |
vaktā sarvasya guhyasya tvadanyo naiva vidyate || 10-6 ||
1.2.d:
किमर्थं किंमयं देव तन्मे विस्तरशो वद |
वक्ता सर्वस्य गुह्यस्य त्वदन्यो नैव विद्यते || 10-6 ||
1.2.m:
For what purpose and consisting of what is it, O god? Tell me that in detail.
No other speaker of every secret exists than you. // 10-6
Determination to explain measure

1.2.s:
śṛṇu nārada tattvena pramāṇasthitimavyayām |
viśvaṃ yatraiva viśrāntaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam || 10-7 ||
1.2.d:
शृणु नारद तत्त्वेन प्रमाणस्थितिमव्ययाम् |
विश्वं यत्रैव विश्रान्तं सदेवासुरमानुषम् || 10-7 ||
1.2.m:
Listen, O Nārada, truly to the imperishable state of measure,
wherein the universe rests together with gods, asuras, and humans. // 10-7
Explanation of the nature of measure

1.2.s:
madhyamo yaḥ sa saṃkalpo viṣṇoḥ sṛṣṭavato jagat |
śāśvate tiṣṭhati vyaktaṃ jaganmārga itīdṛśaḥ || 10-8 ||
1.2.d:
मध्यमो यः स संकल्पो विष्णोः सृष्टवतो जगत् |
शाश्वते तिष्ठति व्यक्तं जगन्मार्ग इतीदृशः || 10-8 ||
1.2.m:
That intermediate will of Viṣṇu who has created the universe,
stands manifestly in the eternal [realm]: such is the path of the world. // 10-8
That is declared to be measure, the wheel of maintenance, O great sage. // 10-9ab
It is conceived as twofold by way of aggregate and individual component. // 10-9cd
Nature of the aggregate measure

1.2.s:
aikarūpyeṇa saṃkalpo yaḥ sarvaviṣaye sthitaḥ |
mahāsthitimayaṃ cakraṃ tadetat kīrtitaṃ mune || 10-10 ||
1.2.d:
ऐकरूप्येण संकल्पो यः सर्वविषये स्थितः |
महास्थितिमयं चक्रं तदेतत् कीर्तितं मुने || 10-10 ||
1.2.m:
The will which resides uniformly with respect to all objects,
that is celebrated as the wheel consisting of great maintenance, O sage. // 10-10
Nature of the individual measure

1.2.s:
tattveyattā samastātman yasminnāyatate'khilā |
prātisvikī vyavasthā yā yasya sattvasya yādṛśī || 10-11 ||
1.2.d:
तत्त्वेयत्ता समस्तात्मन् यस्मिन्नायततेऽखिला |
प्रातिस्विकी व्यवस्था या यस्य सत्त्वस्य यादृशी || 10-11 ||
1.2.m:
O all-pervading soul, in which the entire limitation of principles extends,
whatever particular order belongs to whichever being, of whatever kind, // 10-11

1.2.s:
p. 89) pariṇāmakriyāsādhyasthānarūpādigocarā |
tadvadvyaṣṭimaye cakre pramāṇe sā vyavasthitā || 10-12 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 89) परिणामक्रियासाध्यस्थानरूपादिगोचरा |
तद्वद्व्यष्टिमये चक्रे प्रमाणे सा व्यवस्थिता || 10-12 ||
1.2.m:
pertaining to transformation, action, what is to be effected, place, form, and so on,
in that same way it is established in measure as the wheel consisting of individual components. // 10-12

1.2.s:
ekaceṣṭādiko yortho yaśca sṛṣṭyādilakṣaṇaḥ |
śāstraśāstrārthatatsādhyavyavasthātmā ca yo mune || 10-13 ||
1.2.d:
एकचेष्टादिको योर्थो यश्च सृष्ट्यादिलक्षणः |
शास्त्रशास्त्रार्थतत्साध्यव्यवस्थात्मा च यो मुने || 10-13 ||
1.2.m:
Whatever purpose beginning with a single exertion, and whatever is characterized by creation and so on,
and whatever has the nature of order regarding scripture, the meaning of scripture, and what is to be accomplished by it, O sage, // 10-13
which arises from respective will in the emanation beginning with Vāsudeva, // 10-14ab
[is] the measure by which all that attains its limitation. // 10-14cd
Detailed explanation of that very thing
And that which is the supreme space, characterized by divine enjoyment, // 10-15ab

1.2.s:
sthitipramāṇarūpeṇa tatsaṃkalpena vai hareḥ |
aniyattamasaṃkocamanantaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate || 10-16 ||
1.2.d:
स्थितिप्रमाणरूपेण तत्संकल्पेन वै हरेः |
अनियत्तमसंकोचमनन्तं व्यवतिष्ठते || 10-16 ||
1.2.m:
by Hari's will in the form of the measure of maintenance,
abides indeed unlimited, uncontracted, and infinite. // 10-16

1.2.s:
acetanānāṃ tattvānāṃ yā sā yoniḥ parā mune |
kālakālyamayī śaktiriyattā tattridhā parā || 10-17 ||
1.2.d:
अचेतनानां तत्त्वानां या सा योनिः परा मुने |
कालकाल्यमयी शक्तिरियत्ता तत्त्रिधा परा || 10-17 ||
1.2.m:
That which is the supreme womb of insentient principles, O sage,
the power consisting of time and what is to be driven, limitation [therein] is threefold and supreme. // 10-17

1.2.s:
svarūpakāryabhāvādau sā pramāṇanibandhanā |
niyatiḥ kāla ityete dve kālasya bhide mate || 10-18 ||
1.2.d:
स्वरूपकार्यभावादौ सा प्रमाणनिबन्धना |
नियतिः काल इत्येते द्वे कालस्य भिदे मते || 10-18 ||
1.2.m:
In intrinsic nature, effect, state of being, and so forth, it is bound by measure.
Destiny and time: these are considered two divisions of time. // 10-18

1.2.s:
śuddhāśuddhamaye madhye yaḥ pumān kūṭavat sthitaḥ |
nānājīvamahāyonistasya yā sthitiravyayā || 10-19 ||
1.2.d:
शुद्धाशुद्धमये मध्ये यः पुमान् कूटवत् स्थितः |
नानाजीवमहायोनिस्तस्य या स्थितिरव्यया || 10-19 ||
1.2.m:
The Puruṣa who stands like an anvil in the midst of the pure and the impure,
the great womb of manifold living beings—his imperishable maintenance, // 10-19

1.2.s:
p. 90) iyattā yā ca sā cakre pramāṇe vyavatiṣṭhate |
iyattāyā bhidā yā ca kalākāṣṭhādigocarā || 10-20 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 90) इयत्ता या च सा चक्रे प्रमाणे व्यवतिष्ठते |
इयत्ताया भिदा या च कलाकाष्ठादिगोचरा || 10-20 ||
1.2.m:
and whatever limitation [it has], stands in the wheel of measure.
And whatever division of limitation pertains to digits, minutes, and so forth, // 10-20

1.2.s:
sā pramāṇamaye cakre sarvāpyāyatate mune |
sattvādīnāṃ svarūpaṃ yadyā pravṛttiḥ phalaṃ ca yat || 10-21 ||
1.2.d:
सा प्रमाणमये चक्रे सर्वाप्यायतते मुने |
सत्त्वादीनां स्वरूपं यद्या प्रवृत्तिः फलं च यत् || 10-21 ||
1.2.m:
all that extends within the wheel consisting of measure, O sage.
Whatever is the intrinsic nature of goodness and the other [qualities], whatever their activity and whatever their fruit, // 10-21

1.2.s:
iyattā tatra sarvatra sā pramāṇasudarśanāt |
yadrūpatritayaṃ buddherdharmādyā yā ca vikriyā || 10-22 ||
1.2.d:
इयत्ता तत्र सर्वत्र सा प्रमाणसुदर्शनात् |
यद्रूपत्रितयं बुद्धेर्धर्माद्या या च विक्रिया || 10-22 ||
1.2.m:
the limitation everywhere therein is from Sudarśana as measure.
Whatever is the triad of forms of the intellect, and whatever transformation beginning with virtue, // 10-22

1.2.s:
vyāpāraspandanirṇītirnimeṣātmā ca yo'khilaḥ |
yo'treyattāmayo bhāvaḥ sa pramāṇasudarśanāt || 10-23 ||
1.2.d:
व्यापारस्पन्दनिर्णीतिर्निमेषात्मा च योऽखिलः |
योऽत्रेयत्तामयो भावः स प्रमाणसुदर्शनात् || 10-23 ||
1.2.m:
activity, vibration, determination, and all that has the nature of a twinkling of an eye—
whatever state of being consists of limitation here is from Sudarśana as measure. // 10-23

1.2.s:
abhimāno dvidhā yo'pi saṃrambho yo'pyahaṃkṛteḥ |
yaśca kāmādiko bhāvastatreyattāsthitiśca yā || 10-24 ||
1.2.d:
अभिमानो द्विधा योऽपि संरम्भो योऽप्यहंकृतेः |
यश्च कामादिको भावस्तत्रेयत्तास्थितिश्च या || 10-24 ||
1.2.m:
Whatever twofold self-conceit and whatever impetuosity of the ego-sense,
and whatever state of being beginning with desire, and whatever maintenance of limitation therein, // 10-24

1.2.s:
sā pramāṇamaye cakre saṃkalpe'smin sudarśanena |
pañcānāṃ pañcakaṃ yacca saṃkalpānāmavasthitam || 10-25 ||
1.2.d:
सा प्रमाणमये चक्रे संकल्पेऽस्मिन् सुदर्शनेन |
पञ्चानां पञ्चकं यच्च संकल्पानामवस्थितम् || 10-25 ||
1.2.m:
that is in this will consisting of the wheel of measure by Sudarśana.
And whatever pentad of the five resolves is established, // 10-25

1.2.s:
tādṛśaṃ ca vikalpānāṃ tadetad dvitayaṃ mune |
iyattā yā sthitā vyāpya sā pramāṇasudarśanāt || 10-26 ||
1.2.d:
तादृशं च विकल्पानां तदेतद् द्वितयं मुने |
इयत्ता या स्थिता व्याप्य सा प्रमाणसुदर्शनात् || 10-26 ||
1.2.m:
and likewise of doubts—this pair, O sage,
and the limitation which stands pervading them, is from Sudarśana as measure. // 10-26

1.2.s:
tānavaṃ pāṭavaṃ yacca yaccālocanapañcakam |
śāntaghorādikaṃ rūpaṃ yacca dhīndriyapañcake || 10-27 ||
1.2.d:
तानवं पाटवं यच्च यच्चालोचनपञ्चकम् |
शान्तघोरादिकं रूपं यच्च धीन्द्रियपञ्चके || 10-27 ||
1.2.m:
Whatever weakness, keenness, and whatever pentad of perceptions,
and whatever form beginning with peaceful and fierce in the pentad of sensory faculties; // 10-27

1.2.s:
vacanādānavikrāntimodotsargamayaṃ ca yat |
śāntaghorādikaṃ rūpaṃ yatkarmendriyapañcake || 10-28 ||
1.2.d:
वचनादानविक्रान्तिमोदोत्सर्गमयं च यत् |
शान्तघोरादिकं रूपं यत्कर्मेन्द्रियपञ्चके || 10-28 ||
1.2.m:
and whatever consists of speaking, taking, moving, pleasure, and excretion,
and whatever form beginning with peaceful and fierce in the pentad of motor faculties; // 10-28

1.2.s:
p. 91) tatreyattāmayaṃ rūpam yacca sthitimayaṃ vapuḥ |
pramāṇe vaiṣṇave sarvaṃ tatsaṃkalpasudarśane || 10-29 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 91) तत्रेयत्तामयं रूपम् यच्च स्थितिमयं वपुः |
प्रमाणे वैष्णवे सर्वं तत्संकल्पसुदर्शने || 10-29 ||
1.2.m:
the form consisting of limitation therein and the body consisting of maintenance,
all that is in the Vaiṣṇava measure, Sudarśana as his will. // 10-29

Aggregate, space, lightness, movement, impulsion, and drying;
also aggregate, space, manifest wetness, viscosity, and minuteness; // 10-30

and stability and earthy hardness—this is the elemental body.
The maintenance consisting of an aggregate of one, two, three, four, and five qualities, // 10-31

1.2.s:
yaistadvyāpya sthiteyattā sā pramāṇasudarśanāt |
tattve tattve ca maryādā yā yā śaśvadavasthitā || 10-32 ||
1.2.d:
यैस्तद्व्याप्य स्थितेयत्ता सा प्रमाणसुदर्शनात् |
तत्त्वे तत्त्वे च मर्यादा या या शश्वदवस्थिता || 10-32 ||
1.2.m:
the limitation by which they stand pervaded, is from Sudarśana as measure.
And whatever boundary is permanently established in each principle, // 10-32

1.2.s:
sā sā pramāṇacakrasya saṃkalpasya harergatiḥ |
itīyaṃ sthitimaryādeyattā cakre prakīrtitā || 10-33 ||
1.2.d:
सा सा प्रमाणचक्रस्य संकल्पस्य हरेर्गतिः |
इतीयं स्थितिमर्यादेयत्ता चक्रे प्रकीर्तिता || 10-33 ||
1.2.m:
that very one is the course of Hari's will, the wheel of measure.
Thus this limitation, the boundary of maintenance, has been proclaimed in the wheel. // 10-33

1.2.s:
viṣṇusaṃkalpasaṃbhūtāṃ sthitimanyāṃ mune śṛṇu |
pratibandhanirāsena yā svabhāvagatirmune || 10-34 ||
1.2.d:
विष्णुसंकल्पसंभूतां स्थितिमन्यां मुने शृणु |
प्रतिबन्धनिरासेन या स्वभावगतिर्मुने || 10-34 ||
1.2.m:
Hear another maintenance, O sage, born of Viṣṇu's will:
that course of intrinsic nature through the removal of obstacles, O sage, // 10-34

1.2.s:
tattvānāṃ tāttvikānāṃ ca sā sthitiḥ kathyate mune |
guṇāntarānugraheṇa yaḥ sattvonmeṣa ūrjitaḥ || 10-35 ||
1.2.d:
तत्त्वानां तात्त्विकानां च सा स्थितिः कथ्यते मुने |
गुणान्तरानुग्रहेण यः सत्त्वोन्मेष ऊर्जितः || 10-35 ||
1.2.m:
is called the maintenance of principles and things derived from principles, O sage.
The powerful emergence of goodness through the favor of other qualities, // 10-35

consisting of virtue, knowledge, and so on, is impelled by Sudarśana.
That particular measure is to be understood as the upholder of the three worlds. // 10-36

Being gradually practiced by those whose intellects are illumined by goodness,
it constantly supports heaven and earth through the gift of food, rain, and so forth. // 10-37

1.2.s:
p. 92) guṇāntarānugraheṇa tamaso yaḥ sa udyamaḥ |
adharmādisvarūpo'sau viṣṇusaṃkalpacoditaḥ || 10-38 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 92) गुणान्तरानुग्रहेण तमसो यः स उद्यमः |
अधर्मादिस्वरूपोऽसौ विष्णुसंकल्पचोदितः || 10-38 ||
1.2.m:
That exertion of darkness through the favor of other qualities,
consisting of vice and the like, is urged by Viṣṇu's will. // 10-38

Being gradually practiced by those whose intellects are stained by darkness,
it destroys heaven and earth through the destruction of food, rain, and so forth. // 10-39
Affliction of goodness is constant from the pair of qualities other than it. // 10-40ab
Explanation of the array of weapons
Then, intending to cast down the unrighteous in order to establish righteousness, // 10-40cd

1.2.s:
janārdanatvamīśāno yadā viṣṇuḥ prapadyate |
tadā devasya saṃkalpaḥ sudarśanasamāhvayaḥ || 10-41 ||
1.2.d:
जनार्दनत्वमीशानो यदा विष्णुः प्रपद्यते |
तदा देवस्य संकल्पः सुदर्शनसमाह्वयः || 10-41 ||
1.2.m:
when sovereign Viṣṇu assumes the state of Janārdana,
then the will of the god, named Sudarśana, // 10-41

assumes embodied form in the nature of weapons and the like:
in the form of the discus, plow, Saunanda [club], conch, Śārṅga bow, and arrows; // 10-42

in the form of sword and shield, with noose, goad, and axes;
in the nature of staff and spear, in the form of thunderbolt and pestle; // 10-43

in the form of the hundred-pointed fire, in the nature of lance and power-dart;
likewise in the form of the trident, and in the form of weapons beginning with the skull-topped staff. // 10-44

1.2.s:
evaṃ nānāvidhai rūpaistatsaṃkalpavikalpitaiḥ |
udeti jagato vṛddhyai nārāyaṇakarāśrayī || 10-45 ||
1.2.d:
एवं नानाविधै रूपैस्तत्संकल्पविकल्पितैः |
उदेति जगतो वृद्ध्यै नारायणकराश्रयी || 10-45 ||
1.2.m:
Thus, in manifold forms devised by his will,
resting in Nārāyaṇa's hand, he arises for the prosperity of the universe. // 10-45

1.2.s:
iti śastramayo vyūho leśataste nidarśitaḥ |
aparo'stramayo vyūhaḥ saudarśana udīryate || 10-46 ||
1.2.d:
इति शस्त्रमयो व्यूहो लेशतस्ते निदर्शितः |
अपरोऽस्त्रमयो व्यूहः सौदर्शन उदीर्यते || 10-46 ||
1.2.m: Thus the weapon-consisting array has been shown to you in brief; / another array, consisting of missile-weapons, belonging to Sudarśana, is [now] declared: // 10-46
[p. 93] Demonstration of the missile-weapon array
Assuming a divine form whose limbs and secondary limbs are its ornaments, / in the manner of Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and the rest from his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet, // 10-47
for the protection of everything, he emits the array consisting of the missile of Brahmā and the rest, / bringing forward and turning back, accepted as sixty-twofold. // 10-48

1.2.s:
prajāpatipitṛbrahmadevebhyaśca tathā tathā |
divyo nānāvidhākāraḥ samudetyastrarūpavān || 10-49 ||
1.2.d:
प्रजापतिपितृब्रह्मदेवेभ्यश्च तथा तथा |
दिव्यो नानाविधाकारः समुदेत्यस्त्ररूपवान् || 10-49 ||
1.2.m: And likewise from the Prajāpatis, ancestors, Brahmās, and gods, / the divine one, of manifold forms, arises possessing the form of missile-weapons. // 10-49
Even among Brahmin-seers, divine seers, and royal seers, who consist of mantras, / he abides solely in the form of imprecations, curses, and the like. // 10-50

1.2.s:
na tadasti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi vā munisattama |
nigrahe'nugrahe vāpi yatrāyaṃ naiva sādhanam || 10-51 ||
1.2.d:
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि वा मुनिसत्तम |
निग्रहेऽनुग्रहे वापि यत्रायं नैव साधनम् || 10-51 ||
1.2.m: There is nothing on earth or in heaven, best of sages, / in restraint or in grace, wherein this [discus] is not the means. // 10-51

1.2.s:
pramāṇavyūha etāvānarthākāro nidarśitaḥ |
sudarśanasya devasya śabdākāramatho śṛṇu || 10-52 ||
1.2.d:
प्रमाणव्यूह एतावानर्थाकारो निदर्शितः |
सुदर्शनस्य देवस्य शब्दाकारमथो शृणु || 10-52 ||
1.2.m: This measure-array, having the form of objects, has been shown to such an extent; / hear now the sound-form of god Sudarśana. // 10-52

1.2.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyām
arthātmakapramāṇavyūhanirūpaṇaṃ nāma
daśamo'dhyāyāḥ || 10 ||
1.2.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायाम्
अर्थात्मकप्रमाणव्यूहनिरूपणं नाम
दशमोऽध्यायाः || 10 ||
1.2.m: Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled 'Determination of the Measure-Array Consisting of Objects', in the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā of the secret teaching of the glorious Pāñcarātra. // 10
Chapter Eleven, titled 'Determination of the Measure-Array Consisting of Sound'

1.2.s:
namaḥ samastagīrvāṇasukhasaubhāgyadāyine |
śaṃkarāya girīśāya gaurīdayita te namaḥ || 11-1 ||
1.2.d:
नमः समस्तगीर्वाणसुखसौभाग्यदायिने |
शंकराय गिरीशाय गौरीदयित ते नमः || 11-1 ||
1.2.m: Homage to the giver of happiness and good fortune to all the gods; / homage to Śaṃkara, the lord of the mountain, the beloved of Gaurī! // 11-1
Inquiry into the measure consisting of sound

1.2.s:
śrutaḥ pramāṇarūpo'yaṃ vyūhārtho yanmayākhilaḥ |
śabdākāro ya uddiṣṭastaṃ me vada sureśvara || 11-2 ||
1.2.d:
श्रुतः प्रमाणरूपोऽयं व्यूहार्थो यन्मयाखिलः |
शब्दाकारो य उद्दिष्टस्तं मे वद सुरेश्वर || 11-2 ||
1.2.m: Since this entire object of the array having the form of measure has been heard by me, / tell me, lord of gods, that which was indicated as having the form of sound. // 11-2
Introduction with the intention of explaining that

1.2.s:
ādisarge purāvṛtte nānābhāvavibhūṣite |
āsīcchaktimato viṣṇoriyaṃ cintā sukhodayā || 11-3 ||
1.2.d:
आदिसर्गे पुरावृत्ते नानाभावविभूषिते |
आसीच्छक्तिमतो विष्णोरियं चिन्ता सुखोदया || 11-3 ||
1.2.m: When the primal creation occurred in the past, adorned with manifold states of being, / this thought, bringing forth happiness, arose in Viṣṇu the possessor of Śakti: // 11-3
The manner of the Lord's thought at the primal creation

1.2.s:
vipuleyaṃ kṛtā sṛṣṭirmayā sattvaguṇottarā |
pratyakṣasarvadharmārthā nirābādhā sukhottarā || 11-4 ||
1.2.d:
विपुलेयं कृता सृष्टिर्मया सत्त्वगुणोत्तरा |
प्रत्यक्षसर्वधर्मार्था निराबाधा सुखोत्तरा || 11-4 ||
1.2.m: "This vast creation has been made by me, abundant in the quality of sattva, / wherein all dharma and wealth are directly perceived, unobstructed, abundant in happiness. // 11-4
These creatures have been produced, thronged with divine seers and Brahmās;
Manifestation of own nature preceded by attainment of the supreme Puruṣa through the increase of sattva
[p. 95] through connection with knowledge of truth, and also through the performance of true dharma, // 11-5

1.2.s: acireṇaiva māṃ prāpya svīyaṃ bhāvaṃ bhajiṣyate |
1.2.d: अचिरेणैव मां प्राप्य स्वीयं भावं भजिष्यते |
1.2.m: having reached me before long, they will enjoy their own state of being.
Diminution of sattva through the increase of rajas and tamas
By time alone there will be an excess of the qualities of rajas and tamas; // 11-6
under the influence of their emergence, sattva will also be dried up.
Then, manifestation of Daityas and others
Then Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas will appear; // 11-7
Subversion of Vedic boundary by them
by them this divine, sāttvic boundary will be shaken.
Disappearance of dharma from the loss of knowledge
When complete knowledge is destroyed by the emergence of the qualities of rajas and tamas, // 11-8
that dharma which is the cause of knowledge will also go to disappearance.
And then these creatures, without support and impure, will perish. // 11-9
Then, the finding of occasion for the descents of the Lord
There, through many forms, I shall have constant work;
[p. 96] in them, there will be a need for manifold kinds of equipment. // 11-10
Determination to establish dharma

1.2.s:
āviśyāviśya bhūtāni svena rūpeṇa māyayā |
taistaiḥ sādhanasaṃbhedairnirasya sukṛtadviṣaḥ || 11-11 ||
1.2.d:
आविश्याविश्य भूतानि स्वेन रूपेण मायया |
तैस्तैः साधनसंभेदैर्निरस्य सुकृतद्विषः || 11-11 ||
1.2.m: Entering beings repeatedly, in my own form through māyā, / having driven off the haters of good deeds by various kinds of means, // 11-11
the boundary of dharma will be made easy to maintain in various places.
Twofold nature of the means to dispel adharma
And the means must be made twofold in dispelling the haters of dharma: // 11-12
in the form of an array of weapons and missile-weapons, and in the form of sacred teaching."
Arising of both from the Lord's will
Having said this, willing an array having the form of objects, filled with a flood of weapons and missile-weapons, // 11-13

1.2.s:
vyūhaṃ sasarja saṃkalpya svena saṃkalpatejasā |
sa ca saudarśano vyūho maryādādhāraṇakṣamaḥ || 11-14 ||
1.2.d:
व्यूहं ससर्ज संकल्प्य स्वेन संकल्पतेजसा |
स च सौदर्शनो व्यूहो मर्यादाधारणक्षमः || 11-14 ||
1.2.m: he emitted it by the fiery energy of his own will; / and that Sudarśana array is capable of upholding the boundary. // 11-14

1.2.s:
pramāṇarūpa uddiṣṭo vakṣyate ca tathā tathā |
pramāṇarūpaśāstrārthaḥ saṃkalpo vaiṣṇavo hi yaḥ || 11-15 ||
1.2.d:
प्रमाणरूप उद्दिष्टो वक्ष्यते च तथा तथा |
प्रमाणरूपशास्त्रार्थः संकल्पो वैष्णवो हि यः || 11-15 ||
1.2.m: It has been indicated as having the form of measure, and it will be explained in various ways. / For that will belonging to Viṣṇu, whose purpose is the sacred teaching having the form of measure, // 11-15
arose from that Brahman—grasp how it did so.
Description of the nature of the primal sacred teaching
Consisting solely of will, single, dispelling all inner darkness, // 11-16

1.2.s:
p. 97) nirghātaśabdavadvyomnaḥ śāstramekamabhūt tadā |
varṇārthaiḥ saṃbhṛtairvarnaiścidānandamahormibhiḥ || 11-17 ||
1.2.d:
प्. 97) निर्घातशब्दवद्व्योम्नः शास्त्रमेकमभूत् तदा |
वर्णार्थैः संभृतैर्वर्नैश्चिदानन्दमहोर्मिभिः || 11-17 ||
1.2.m: [p. 97] like the sound of a thunderstroke, one sacred teaching then arose from space, / with the phonemes laden with phonemic meanings, with great waves of consciousness and bliss, // 11-17

1.2.d:
विष्णुशक्तिसमुद्रोत्थैर्मणिभिमाक्तिकैरिव |
प्रोतं सौदर्शनं रूपं विष्णोः संकल्पकल्पितम् || 11-18 ||
1.2.m: as if with pearls, jewels risen from the ocean of Viṣṇu's power, / strung together in the form of Sudarśana, devised by Viṣṇu's will. // 11-18

1.2.s:
tadvijñānamayaṃ śāstraṃ saddharmapratipādakam |
niyutādhyāyi yat proktaṃ kāmapālena śāśvatam || 11-19 ||
1.2.d:
तद्विज्ञानमयं शास्त्रं सद्धर्मप्रतिपादकम् |
नियुताध्यायि यत् प्रोक्तं कामपालेन शाश्वतम् || 11-19 ||
1.2.m: That sacred teaching consisting of discernment, setting forth true dharma, / which was proclaimed as eternal with one hundred thousand chapters by Kāmapāla, // 11-19
Its containing the meaning of all sacred teachings
endowed with the four human ends, filled with reasons, / served by the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma, and by the Angirases and Atharvans, // 11-20
strewn with many varieties of words, sentences, and measure-meanings, / adorned with various auspicious conventions, divine and human, // 11-21
encompassed by diverse metres devised through those rituals, / with tenses, voice-markers, numbers, roots, affixes, accents, // 11-22

1.2.s:
vibhaktikārakairliṅgaiḥ svairaiḥ prakṛtisandhibhiḥ |
saṃjñābhiḥ sādhikārābhirbhūṣitaṃ paribhāṣayā || 11-23 ||
1.2.d:
विभक्तिकारकैर्लिङ्गैः स्वैरैः प्रकृतिसन्धिभिः |
संज्ञाभिः साधिकाराभिर्भूषितं परिभाषया || 11-23 ||
1.2.m: case endings, case roles, genders, free euphonic combinations of roots, / technical terms, governing rules, and adorned with interpretive metarules. // 11-23
with substitutions, augments, elisions, modifications, and secondary conditions, / and with various compound formations, sentences, and attendant words, // 11-24
with indeclinables, prefixes, nouns, verbs, and particles, / with the forces of moraic metres and accents, and with formulas of pronunciation, // 11-25

1.2.s:
yamaraṅgavibhāgaiśca bhūṣitaṃ padabhaṅgibhiḥ |
varṇāgamavikalpaiśca tathā varṇaviparyayaiḥ || 11-26 ||
1.2.d:
यमरङ्गविभागैश्च भूषितं पदभङ्गिभिः |
वर्णागमविकल्पैश्च तथा वर्णविपर्ययैः || 11-26 ||
1.2.m: with divisions into twin letters and nasalizations, adorned with stylistic turns of words, / and with variations in the augment of phonemes as well as inversions of phonemes, // 11-26
and with concise formulations of modification and of original base, / with diverse etymological treatises and manifold conclusions, // 11-27
with variations arising from calculations based on planets, lunar mansions, and zodiacal signs, / and with variations of the horary division and rules devised according to results, // 11-28

with investigations arising from injunctions, explanatory passages, and mantras, and conceptions of rituals, / with the application of subsidiary elements, sequential orders, and deductive reasonings, and with general applications, inclusions, and extended applications, // 11-29

with manifold qualifications, and investigations whose domain is the sentence, / with logical maxims formulated by measures [of knowledge], and with clinchers, quibbles, and futile rejoinders, // 11-30
with varieties of substances and actions, and conceptions of qualities and universals, / with variations in the functions of the four priests, and displays of the fourfold Veda, // 11-31
with rules for the four stages of life, and distinctions among the four social classes, / with various rules for consecrations, and sequences of obligatory and optional rites, // 11-32

1.2.s:
itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ vividhābhyāṃ samanvitam |
vividhaiśca prasaṃkhyānaiḥ svaprakṛtyādikalpitaiḥ || 11-33 ||
1.2.d:
इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां विविधाभ्यां समन्वितम् |
विविधैश्च प्रसंख्यानैः स्वप्रकृत्यादिकल्पितैः || 11-33 ||
1.2.m: accompanied by diverse epics and Purāṇas, / and with diverse enumerations devised through one's own primal nature and the like, // 11-33
variegated by distinctions regarding the soul and the Lord, by variations regarding transformation, / and by formulations of properties, temporal states, and definitions, // 11-34

accompanied by manifold conceptions of the measures [of knowledge] along with their creations, / and by investigations into adhesion and non-adhesion whose domain is the spirit and the unmanifest, // 11-35
with conceptions of principles and their owners, reflections on various states, / investigations into the stages of liberation, and manifold conceptions of apprehension, // 11-36
with examinations of the merits and defects designated as knowledge and ignorance, / variations of the three qualities, and reflections on creation and conjunction, // 11-37

1.2.s:
ānvitaṃ vividhaiḥ sāṃkhyaiḥ prasaṃkhyānakṛtakramaiḥ |
yogaprakārakalpaiśca vṛttīnāṃ kalpanairapi || 11-38 ||
1.2.d:
आन्वितं विविधैः सांख्यैः प्रसंख्यानकृतक्रमैः |
योगप्रकारकल्पैश्च वृत्तीनां कल्पनैरपि || 11-38 ||
1.2.m: accompanied by various Sāṃkhya systems whose sequences are established through enumeration, / and by conceptions of the types of yoga and formulations of the mental fluctuations, // 11-38
with various conceptions of practice, formulations of the fourfold dispassion, / and reflections on the internal and external limbs of yoga, // 11-39
with descriptions of afflictions, karmic actions, fruit-maturations, and karmic deposits, / and with reflections on afflictive impressions and examinations of the varieties of suffering, // 11-40

1.2.s:
taistaiścaturadhiṣṭhānakalpanaiḥ kalpitaṃ pṛthak |
upādeyasya heyasya hānopādānayorapi || 11-41 ||
1.2.d:
तैस्तैश्चतुरधिष्ठानकल्पनैः कल्पितं पृथक् |
उपादेयस्य हेयस्य हानोपादानयोरपि || 11-41 ||
1.2.m: distinctly devised through various conceptions of the four foundations— / of that which is to be adopted, that which is to be rejected, and of rejection and adoption— // 11-41
with diverse reflections on the essential nature [of things], conceptions of experience and desire,
and manifold yogas of action which are means for purifying the mind, // 11-42
and adorned with extraordinary supernatural powers situated in the mind; / with variations in the exposition of the Lord, the fetter, and the bound beast, diversified by logical grounds, // 11-43
with conceptions of the pure path according to the division into action and knowledge, / adorned with manifold reflections on the five topics, // 11-44
with reflections on the five powers, examinations of the three impurities, / descriptions of the instruments of experience, conceptions of the forms of embodied souls, // 11-45
with procedures for initiation and installation, and also with Pāśupata observances— / thus, through a variety of intellectual conceptions of diverse forms, // 11-46

1.3.s:
yuktaṃ kalpanayā śaśvat kḷptanānādhikārayā |
adhikāreṇa saddharmān vyācakṣāṇamanekadhā || 11-47 ||
1.3.d:
युक्तं कल्पनया शश्वत् कॢप्तनानाधिकारया |
अधिकारेण सद्धर्मान् व्याचक्षाणमनेकधा || 11-47 ||
1.3.m: endowed eternally with formulation whose diverse qualifications are established, / expounding true dharmas in many ways in accordance with qualification. // 11-47

1.3.s:
niyutādhyāyakaṃ pūrvamāsīt saṃkarṣaṇoditam |
saṃkalpamayamādyasya viṣṇoḥ saṃkalpajāt kila || 11-48 ||
1.3.d:
नियुताध्यायकं पूर्वमासीत् संकर्षणोदितम् |
संकल्पमयमाद्यस्य विष्णोः संकल्पजात् किल || 11-48 ||
1.3.m: Formerly, there was [a sacred teaching] of one hundred thousand chapters spoken by Saṃkarṣaṇa, / consisting of the will of the primal Viṣṇu, born indeed from [His] will. // 11-48
The fact that that sacred teaching was the cause of pleasing the Lord

1.3.s:
tena śāstreṇa te divyā manavo mānavāśca te |
ye proktā ādisarge te tathā mānavamānavāḥ || 11-49 ||
1.3.d:
तेन शास्त्रेण ते दिव्या मनवो मानवाश्च ते |
ये प्रोक्ता आदिसर्गे ते तथा मानवमानवाः || 11-49 ||
1.3.m: By means of that sacred teaching, those divine Manus, those humans / who were proclaimed in the primal creation, and likewise the human-descendants of Manu // 11-49
gratified Nārāyaṇa with abundant virtuous actions.
The slow dissemination of that sacred teaching
Then, due to the inversion of time, when the change of yugas arose, // 11-50

1.3.s:
p. 101) tretādau sattvasaṃkocādrajasi pravijṛmbhite |
kāmaṃ kāmayamāneṣu brāhmaṇeṣu mahātmasu || 11-51 ||
1.3.d:
प्. 101) त्रेतादौ सत्त्वसंकोचाद्रजसि प्रविजृम्भिते |
कामं कामयमानेषु ब्राह्मणेषु महात्मसु || 11-51 ||
1.3.m: at the beginning of Tretā, when sattva contracted and rajas flourished, / and when the great-souled brāhmaṇas desired pleasure, // 11-51
that command which belongs to Sudarśana had little circulation.
The division of that sacred teaching by Vācyāyana and others
Then, when the world was confounded by delusion, the regulators of the world-order, // 11-52

1.3.s:
saṃbhūya lokakartāraḥ kartavyaṃ samacintayan |
apāntaratapā nāma munirvāksaṃbhavo hareḥ || 11-53 ||
1.3.d:
संभूय लोककर्तारः कर्तव्यं समचिन्तयन् |
अपान्तरतपा नाम मुनिर्वाक्संभवो हरेः || 11-53 ||
1.3.m: the makers of the world, assembled and reflected on what was to be done: / the sage named Apāntaratapas, born from the speech of Hari; // 11-53

1.3.s:
kapilaśca purāṇarṣirādidevasamudbhavaḥ |
hiraṇyagarbho lokādirahaṃ paśupatiḥ śivaḥ || 11-54 ||
1.3.d:
कपिलश्च पुराणर्षिरादिदेवसमुद्भवः |
हिरण्यगर्भो लोकादिरहं पशुपतिः शिवः || 11-54 ||
1.3.m: Kapila, the ancient seer arisen from the primal god; / Hiraṇyagarbha, the beginning of the world; and I, Paśupati, Śiva. // 11-54

1.3.s:
ete taptvā tapastīvraṃ varṣāṇāmayutaṃ śatam |
ādidevamanujñāpya devadevena coditāḥ || 11-55 ||
1.3.d:
एते तप्त्वा तपस्तीव्रं वर्षाणामयुतं शतम् |
आदिदेवमनुज्ञाप्य देवदेवेन चोदिताः || 11-55 ||
1.3.m: These, having performed severe asceticism for a thousand times a hundred years, / obtained permission from the primal god, and impelled by the God of gods, // 11-55

1.3.s:
sudarśanasya leśena tatsaṃkalpena saṃyutāḥ |
vijñānabalamāsādya dharmāddevaprasādajāt || 11-56 ||
1.3.d:
सुदर्शनस्य लेशेन तत्संकल्पेन संयुताः |
विज्ञानबलमासाद्य धर्माद्देवप्रसादजात् || 11-56 ||
1.3.m: endowed with a portion of Sudarśana and with His will, / having attained the strength of discriminative knowledge from dharma born of divine grace, // 11-56
we carved down that sacred teaching which had appeared, part by part.
Therein, the division of the Veda by Vācyāyana
First, the venerable sage Apāntaratapas carved [his share], // 11-57

1.3.s:
harervācyāyanaḥ putro yāvadāttaṃ ca vai tataḥ |
udabhūt tatra dhīrūpamṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃkulam || 11-58 ||
1.3.d:
हरेर्वाच्यायनः पुत्रो यावदात्तं च वै ततः |
उदभूत् तत्र धीरूपमृग्यजुःसामसंकुलम् || 11-58 ||
1.3.m: Vācyāyana, the son of Hari; and whatever was taken from it, / there arose the form of understanding filled with Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman; // 11-58
born from Viṣṇu's will, this was set forth by Vācyāyana.
The division of Sāṃkhya by Kapila
Kapila of noble intellect carved down whatever portion from the sacred teaching; // 11-59
that became the Sāṃkhya sacred teaching, devoted to enumeration.
The division of the Yoga treatise by Hiraṇyagarbha
Whatever Hiraṇyagarbha, the origin of the world, carved from that primal command, // 11-60
that became this divine Yoga instruction, having restraint and other limbs.
The division of the Pāśupata by Śiva
Whatever portion filled with diverse vows I carved from that sacred teaching, // 11-61
that became the one named Pāśupata, which liberates the bound beast from the fetter.
The division of Pāñcarātra by the Lord
From that exclusive divine command consisting of true revelation, // 11-62

1.3.s:
nirmame sāramuddhṛtya svayaṃ viṣṇurasaṃkulam |
tat paravyūhavibhavasvabhāvādinirūpaṇam || 11-63 ||
1.3.d:
निर्ममे सारमुद्धृत्य स्वयं विष्णुरसंकुलम् |
तत् परव्यूहविभवस्वभावादिनिरूपणम् || 11-63 ||
1.3.m: having extracted the essence, Viṣṇu Himself fashioned the unconfused [tradition] / that sets forth the nature and other aspects of the highest, the emanations, and the divine descents, // 11-63

1.3.s:
pañcarātrāhvayaṃ tantraṃ mokṣaikaphalalakṣaṇam |
sudarśanāhvayo yo'sau saṃkalpo vaiṣṇavaḥ paraḥ || 11-64 ||
1.3.d:
पञ्चरात्राह्वयं तन्त्रं मोक्षैकफललक्षणम् |
सुदर्शनाह्वयो योऽसौ संकल्पो वैष्णवः परः || 11-64 ||
1.3.m: the treatise named Pañcarātra, defined by liberation as its sole fruit. / That supreme Vaiṣṇava will named Sudarśana, // 11-64

1.3.s: sa svayaṃ bibhide tena pañcadhā pañcavaktragaḥ |
1.3.d: स स्वयं बिभिदे तेन पञ्चधा पञ्चवक्त्रगः |
1.3.m: entering the five mouths, became divided fivefold by Him.
Conclusion of the chapter's meaning
This measure-array, which has the form of Viṣṇu's will, has been proclaimed.

1.3.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
śabdātmakapramāṇavyūhanirūpaṇaṃ
nāmaikādaśo'dhyāyaḥ || 11 ||
1.3.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
शब्दात्मकप्रमाणव्यूहनिरूपणं
नामैकादशोऽध्यायः || 11 ||

1.3.s:
surāsuragaṇārādhya namaste pārvatīpriya |
tvatprasādācchrutaṃ deva divyaṃ tadvaiṣṇavaṃ yaśaḥ || 12-1 ||
1.3.d:
सुरासुरगणाराध्य नमस्ते पार्वतीप्रिय |
त्वत्प्रसादाच्छ्रुतं देव दिव्यं तद्वैष्णवं यशः || 12-1 ||

1.3.s:
yat tadādyaṃ mahacchāstraṃ sudarśanamayaṃ hareḥ |
tasmāt pṛthak pṛthakchāstramāhurvācyāyanādayaḥ || 12-2 ||
1.3.d:
यत् तदाद्यं महच्छास्त्रं सुदर्शनमयं हरेः |
तस्मात् पृथक् पृथक्छास्त्रमाहुर्वाच्यायनादयः || 12-2 ||

1.3.s:
trayī sāṃkhyaṃ tathā yogaśāstraṃ pāśupataṃ tathā |
sāttvataṃ ceti tadrūpaṃ śrotumicchāmyahaṃ prabho || 12-3 ||
1.3.d:
त्रयी सांख्यं तथा योगशास्त्रं पाशुपतं तथा |
सात्त्वतं चेति तद्रूपं श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं प्रभो || 12-3 ||

1.3.s:
śṛṇu nārada tattvena teṣāṃ rūpaṃ pṛthak pṛthak |
saṃkalpo yāvatā viṣṇorbhedena vyavatiṣṭhate || 12-4 ||
1.3.d:
शृणु नारद तत्त्वेन तेषां रूपं पृथक् पृथक् |
संकल्पो यावता विष्णोर्भेदेन व्यवतिष्ठते || 12-4 ||

1.3.s:
tatra trayīmayaṃ rūpamādyaṃ sarvārthadaśanam |
ṛgyajuḥsāmarūpatvāt trayī sā parikīrtitā || 12-5 ||
1.3.d:
तत्र त्रयीमयं रूपमाद्यं सर्वार्थदशनम् |
ऋग्यजुःसामरूपत्वात् त्रयी सा परिकीर्तिता || 12-5 ||

1.3.s:
kāryabhedāt trayītve'pi caturdhā sā prakīrtitā |
ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni hyatharvāṅgirasastathā || 12-6 ||
1.3.d:
कार्यभेदात् त्रयीत्वेऽपि चतुर्धा सा प्रकीर्तिता |
ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि ह्यथर्वाङ्गिरसस्तथा || 12-6 ||

1.3.s:
śataṃ caikā ca śākhāḥ syuryajuṣāmekavartmanām |
sāmnāṃ śākhāḥ sahasraṃ syuḥ pañca śākhā atharvaṇām || 12-
9 ||
1.3.d:
शतं चैका च शाखाः स्युर्यजुषामेकवर्त्मनाम् |
साम्नां शाखाः सहस्रं स्युः पञ्च शाखा अथर्वणाम् || 12-
9 ||

1.3.s:
iyanta eva pratyakṣā āmnāyante maharṣibhiḥ |
smaryante munibhirnityaṃ labdhānujñairmaheśvarāt || 12-10 ||
1.3.d:
इयन्त एव प्रत्यक्षा आम्नायन्ते महर्षिभिः |
स्मर्यन्ते मुनिभिर्नित्यं लब्धानुज्ञैर्महेश्वरात् || 12-10 ||

1.3.s: kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ śikṣā niruktaṃ jyotiṣāṃ gatiḥ || 12-11 ||
1.3.d: कल्पो व्याकरणं शिक्षा निरुक्तं ज्योतिषां गतिः || 12-11 ||

1.3.s:
dharmajñasamayo'rthāśca vedavādotthitāstathā |
nibaddhā cānibaddhā ca saṃskārācārasaṃtatiḥ || 12-13 ||
1.3.d:
धर्मज्ञसमयोऽर्थाश्च वेदवादोत्थितास्तथा |
निबद्धा चानिबद्धा च संस्काराचारसंततिः || 12-13 ||

1.3.s:
vāstuvedo dhanurvedo gāndharvaśca tathā mune |
āyurvedaśca pañcaita upavedāḥ prakīrtitāḥ || 12-15 ||
1.3.d:
वास्तुवेदो धनुर्वेदो गान्धर्वश्च तथा मुने |
आयुर्वेदश्च पञ्चैत उपवेदाः प्रकीर्तिताः || 12-15 ||

1.3.s:
daṇḍanītiśca vārtā ca vidyādvayamidaṃ param |
ekaviṃśatibhedo yaḥ saprakāraḥ prakīrtitaḥ || 12-16 ||
1.3.d:
दण्डनीतिश्च वार्ता च विद्याद्वयमिदं परम् |
एकविंशतिभेदो यः सप्रकारः प्रकीर्तितः || 12-16 ||

1.3.s:
vācyāyanādṛṣeḥ pūrvaṃ viṣṇorvāṇīsamudbhavāt |
trayīrūpeṇa saṃkalpa iyadbhedo vijṛmbhitaḥ || 12-17 ||
1.3.d:
वाच्यायनादृषेः पूर्वं विष्णोर्वाणीसमुद्भवात् |
त्रयीरूपेण संकल्प इयद्भेदो विजृम्भितः || 12-17 ||

1.3.s:
sāṃkhyarūpeṇa saṃkalpo vaiṣṇavaḥ kapilādṛṣeḥ |
udito yādṛśaḥ pūrvaṃ tādṛśaṃ śṛṇu me'khilam || 12-18 ||
1.3.d:
सांख्यरूपेण संकल्पो वैष्णवः कपिलादृषेः |
उदितो यादृशः पूर्वं तादृशं शृणु मेऽखिलम् || 12-18 ||

1.3.s: ṣaṣṭibhedaṃ smṛtaṃ tantraṃ sāṃkhyaṃ nāma mahāmune |
1.3.d: षष्टिभेदं स्मृतं तन्त्रं सांख्यं नाम महामुने |

1.3.s: p. 107) prākṛtaṃ vaikṛtaṃ ceti maṇḍale dve samāsataḥ || 12-19 ||
1.3.d: प्. 107) प्राकृतं वैकृतं चेति मण्डले द्वे समासतः || 12-19 ||

1.3.s:
prākṛtaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tatra dvātriṃśadbhedamiṣyate |
tatrādyaṃ brahmatantraṃ tu dvitīyaṃ puruṣāṅkitam || 12-20 ||
1.3.d:
प्राकृतं मण्डलं तत्र द्वात्रिंशद्भेदमिष्यते |
तत्राद्यं ब्रह्मतन्त्रं तु द्वितीयं पुरुषाङ्कितम् || 12-20 ||

1.3.s:
trīṇi tantrāṇyathānyāni śakterniyatikālayoḥ |
guṇatantrāṇyatha trīṇi tantramakṣarapūrvakam || 12-21 ||
1.3.d:
त्रीणि तन्त्राण्यथान्यानि शक्तेर्नियतिकालयोः |
गुणतन्त्राण्यथ त्रीणि तन्त्रमक्षरपूर्वकम् || 12-21 ||

1.3.s:
prāṇatantramathānyattu kartṛtantramathetarat |
sāmitantramathānyattu jñānatantrāṇi pañca ca || 12-22 ||
1.3.d:
प्राणतन्त्रमथान्यत्तु कर्तृतन्त्रमथेतरत् |
सामितन्त्रमथान्यत्तु ज्ञानतन्त्राणि पञ्च च || 12-22 ||

1.3.s:
kriyātantrāṇi prañcātha mātrātantrāṇi pañca ca |
bhūtatantrāṇi pañceti triṃśad dve ca bhidā imāḥ || 12-23 ||
1.3.d:
क्रियातन्त्राणि प्रञ्चाथ मात्रातन्त्राणि पञ्च च |
भूततन्त्राणि पञ्चेति त्रिंशद् द्वे च भिदा इमाः || 12-23 ||

1.3.s: prākṛtaṃ maṇḍalaṃ proktaṃ vaikṛtaṃ maṇḍalaṃ śṛṇu |
1.3.d: प्राकृतं मण्डलं प्रोक्तं वैकृतं मण्डलं शृणु |

1.3.s:
kṛtyakāṇḍāni pañcādau bhogakāṇḍaṃ tathā'param |
vṛttakāṇḍaṃ tathaikaṃ tu kleśakāṇḍāni pañca ca || 12-25 ||
1.3.d:
कृत्यकाण्डानि पञ्चादौ भोगकाण्डं तथाऽपरम् |
वृत्तकाण्डं तथैकं तु क्लेशकाण्डानि पञ्च च || 12-25 ||

1.3.s:
trīṇi pramāṇakāṇḍāni khyātikāṇḍamataḥ param |
dharmakāṇḍamathaikaṃ ca kāṇḍaṃ vairāgyapūrvakam || 12-26 ||
1.3.d:
त्रीणि प्रमाणकाण्डानि ख्यातिकाण्डमतः परम् |
धर्मकाण्डमथैकं च काण्डं वैराग्यपूर्वकम् || 12-26 ||

1.3.s:
p. 108) athaiśvaryasya kāṇḍaṃ ca guṇakāṇḍamataḥ param |
liṅgakāṇḍamathaikaṃ ca dṛṣṭikāṇḍamataḥ param || 12-27 ||
1.3.d:
प्. 108) अथैश्वर्यस्य काण्डं च गुणकाण्डमतः परम् |
लिङ्गकाण्डमथैकं च दृष्टिकाण्डमतः परम् || 12-27 ||

1.3.s:
ānuśravikakāṇḍaṃ ca duḥkhakāṇḍamataḥ param |
siddhikāṇḍamathaikaṃ ca kāṇḍaṃ kāṣāyavācakam || 12-28 ||
1.3.d:
आनुश्रविककाण्डं च दुःखकाण्डमतः परम् |
सिद्धिकाण्डमथैकं च काण्डं काषायवाचकम् || 12-28 ||

1.3.s:
tathā samayakāṇḍaṃ ca mokṣakāṇḍamataḥ param |
aṣṭāviṃśatibhedaṃ taditthaṃ vikṛtimaṇḍalam || 12-29 ||
1.3.d:
तथा समयकाण्डं च मोक्षकाण्डमतः परम् |
अष्टाविंशतिभेदं तदित्थं विकृतिमण्डलम् || 12-29 ||

1.3.s:
ṣaṣṭhitantrāṇyathaikaikameṣāṃ nānāvidhaṃ mune |
ṣaṣṭitantramidaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ sudarśanamayaṃ hareḥ || 12-30 ||
1.3.d:
षष्ठितन्त्राण्यथैकैकमेषां नानाविधं मुने |
षष्टितन्त्रमिदं सांख्यं सुदर्शनमयं हरेः || 12-30 ||

1.3.s: saṃhitā tu nirodhākhyā tatra dvādaśadhā smṛtā || 12-33 ||
1.3.d: संहिता तु निरोधाख्या तत्र द्वादशधा स्मृता || 12-33 ||

1.3.s:
ādhāratantraṃ yogaṃ ca bahistattvādhikāravat |
riktayogākhyatantraṃ ca pūrṇayogākhyameva ca || 12-35 ||
1.3.d:
आधारतन्त्रं योगं च बहिस्तत्त्वाधिकारवत् |
रिक्तयोगाख्यतन्त्रं च पूर्णयोगाख्यमेव च || 12-35 ||

1.3.s:
siddhiyogākhyayā trīṇi mokṣatantramataḥ param |
iti dvādaśabhedāste nirodhāyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ || 12-36 ||
1.3.d:
सिद्धियोगाख्यया त्रीणि मोक्षतन्त्रमतः परम् |
